definition_zh: 演示的；示范的；（语法）指示的；感情外露的
definition_en: showing or explaining something by visible example; (grammar) pointing out a particular person or thing; openly displaying feelings
core_image: 一只手把物件举到众人眼前，让所有人都看清它的样子
scene: The demonstrative model on the bench let every student see how the pump worked.
sceneCN: 这里 demonstrative 是「演示用的、示范的」（第 1 个义项：把结构摆出来给人看）；句意：长凳上那个演示模型让每个学生都看清了泵如何工作。图中可辨识物件：长凳、透明泵体模型、围坐的学生、指向模型的手。

pos.zh: 演示的；示范的；指示的；感情外露的

senses.title: Shown by visible example
senses.titleCN: 演示的：把做法摆出来
senses.definition: serving to show how something works by displaying it rather than only describing it
senses.definitionCN: 以展示实物或动作、而非只靠描述来说明某物如何运作的
senses.example: The demonstrative model of the engine let visitors see every moving part.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机的演示模型让参观者看到了每一个运动部件。
senses.why: monstrare means 'to show'. The de- prefix intensifies the showing, so a demonstrative thing does not merely mention a process, it puts the process in front of the eyes.
senses.whyCN: monstrare 意为“显示”。de- 前缀加强了这个“显示”，因此 demonstrative 的东西不只是提到某个过程，而是把过程摆到眼睛前面。

senses.title: Teaching by demonstration
senses.titleCN: 示范的：做一遍给你看
senses.definition: using a practical display as the method of teaching or explaining
senses.definitionCN: 以实际操作展示作为教学或解释方法的
senses.example: Her demonstrative style of teaching kept the class awake.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种示范式的教学风格让全班都保持清醒。
senses.why: A demonstration places the action beside the explanation. The suffix -ive marks the quality of showing, so the adjective names a method whose tool is visible action.
senses.whyCN: 示范把动作放在讲解旁边。-ive 标记“显示”的性质，因此这个形容词命名的是一种以可见动作为工具的方法。

senses.title: Grammar: pointing outward
senses.titleCN: 指示的：手指向某一个人或物
senses.definition: in grammar, marking a specific person or thing, as this, that, these and those do
senses.definitionCN: 语法上标记特定的人或物，如 this、that、these、those 所做的那样
senses.example: In 'this book', the word 'this' is a demonstrative adjective.
senses.exampleCN: 在 this book 中，this 是指示形容词。
senses.why: The grammatical sense keeps the literal gesture: a demonstrative word points. deictic pointing and the physical pointing hand share the same monstrare image of directing attention.
senses.whyCN: 语法义保留了字面手势：指示词就是用手一指。语法上的指认与用手指出，共享同一个 monstrare“把注意力引过去”的意象。

senses.title: Openly affectionate
senses.titleCN: 感情外露的：抱一下就看得见
senses.definition: showing love or affection openly through hugs, kisses or warm words
senses.definitionCN: 通过拥抱、亲吻或亲热言语公开表达爱意或亲情的
senses.example: He is a demonstrative father who hugs his children every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个感情外露的父亲，每天早上都要抱抱孩子。
senses.why: The 19th-century extension moves from showing objects to showing feelings. The feeling is treated as something held out in the hand, where others can see it.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的引申从“展示物件”转到“展示情感”。情感被当作拿在手里的东西，别人看得见。这个词的首次记录年代只能大致估计。

senses.title: Publicly expressive of support
senses.titleCN: 公开表露的：把态度摆到台面上
senses.definition: expressing a feeling or attitude openly, especially support or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达某种情感或态度，尤指支持或反对
senses.example: The crowd was demonstrative of its support for the striking workers.
senses.exampleCN: 人群公开表达了对罢工工人的支持。
senses.why: The prepositional pattern demonstrative of takes the showing outward: the attitude is displayed for an audience rather than kept private.
senses.whyCN: demonstrative of 这一介词搭配把“显示”推向外部：态度是给观众看的，而不是留给自己。

senses.title: Law: evidence meant to illustrate
senses.titleCN: 实物演示证据的：用模型说服陪审团
senses.definition: in law, describing evidence such as charts, models or maps that illustrates facts already proven
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指图表、模型或地图等说明已证事实的证据
senses.example: The lawyer used a demonstrative exhibit to show the jury the crash path.
senses.exampleCN: 律师用一件演示性证物向陪审团展示碰撞路径。
senses.why: Demonstrative evidence does not itself prove the fact; it demonstrates it. The word stays close to its root because the exhibit is literally shown to the court.
senses.whyCN: 演示性证据本身并不证明事实，而是把事实演示出来。这个词因此贴近词根，因为证物是字面上“被显示给法庭”的。

senses.title: Explanatory by illustration
senses.titleCN: 图解说明的：让数字变成画面
senses.definition: making an idea clear through a diagram, example or visual aid
senses.definitionCN: 通过图表、例子或视觉辅助手段使观点清楚的
senses.example: The report opens with a demonstrative chart of the yearly changes.
senses.exampleCN: 报告开头是一张说明年度变化的图表。
senses.why: A chart demonstrates when it lets the reader see the relation. The prefix de- adds thoroughness: the showing is complete enough to stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 图表之所以起 demonstrative 的作用，是因为它让读者看见关系。de- 前缀加了“彻底”的意思：显示得足够完整，可以独立说明问题。

senses.title: The noun: a pointing word
senses.titleCN: 名词：指示词本身
senses.definition: a word such as this or those that points to a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 如 this 或 those 那样指向特定事物的词
senses.example: English learners often confuse demonstratives with personal pronouns.
senses.exampleCN: 英语学习者常把指示词与人称代词混淆。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the pointing tool itself. The -ive adjective becomes a noun without changing the gesture: it is the finger, not the thing pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，这个词命名的是“指引工具”本身。-ive 形容词转为名词，手势没变：它是指头，不是被指的东西。

intro.en: Demonstrative descends from Latin monstrare 'to show', a verb built on monstrum 'portent'. The omen showed the will of the gods, so 'showing' and 'warning' were one act. English added -ive to the Latin stem.
intro.cn: demonstrative 源于拉丁动词 monstrare“显示”，而 monstrare 又建立在 monstrum“征兆”之上。征兆显示神的意志，因此“显示”与“警示”原本是同一个动作。英语在拉丁词干后加了 -ive。

items.en: monstrum meant 'a divine omen or portent', generally thought to come from monere 'to warn, advise'. A portent is something that shows itself so that people may take warning.
items.cn: monstrum 意为“神兆、预兆”，一般认为来自 monere“警告、提醒”。预兆就是自己显现出来、让人据此警觉的东西。

items.en: From monstrum came monstrare 'to show, point out'. The verb keeps the idea that what is shown is meant to be noticed and understood, not merely seen.
items.cn: 由 monstrum 派生出 monstrare“显示、指出”。这个动词保留了“被显示之物应当被注意并理解”的观念，而不只是被看见。

items.en: demonstrare adds the intensive de- 'completely' to monstrare, giving 'to show fully, to point out plainly'. The prefix does not mean 'down' here; it strengthens the verb.
items.cn: demonstrare 在 monstrare 前加加强语气的 de-“完全地”，意为“完整地显示、明确地指出”。这里的 de- 不是“向下”，而是加强动词。

items.en: English forms demonstrative on the stem demonstrat- plus -ive, from Latin -ivus 'having the nature of'. The adjective dates from the 14th to 16th century; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语以 demonstrat- 词干加 -ive（来自拉丁 -ivus“具有……性质”）构成 demonstrative。该形容词大致出现于 14 至 16 世纪，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: The grammatical use for this, that, these and those appears in the 16th century. It borrows the physical gesture of pointing: the word does what the finger does.
items.cn: 用于 this、that、these、those 的语法义出现于 16 世纪。它借用了用手一指的物理动作：词做了手指做的事。

items.en: The sense 'openly showing affection' is a 19th-century development. It extends the same image from objects to feelings, which are now held out for others to see.
items.cn: “公开表露感情”这一义项是 19 世纪的引申。它把同一个意象从物件扩展到情感：情感现在被举出来给别人看。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the show-stem but splits by suffix and prefix; the near-meaning group shares the idea of making something visible but differs in what is displayed.
note.cn: 形近组共享“显示”词干，但按后缀和前缀分流；近义组都含“使某物可见”的意思，区别在于展示的对象不同。

entries.definition: able to be proved or shown clearly. The -able suffix means 'capable of being', so the word concerns proof rather than display.
entries.definitionCN: 可证明的；可明确显示的。-able 表示“能够被……”，因此这个词讲的是可证明性，而不是展示。

entries.definition: the act of showing or proving; also a public protest. The -tion suffix turns the action into a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 演示；论证；亦指公开示威。-tion 把动作变成事物。

entries.definition: protesting or objecting. re- 'back' + monstrare 'show' pictures showing something back at someone, hence complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 抗议的；反对的。re-“向后”+ monstrare“显示”，画面是把东西怼回给对方看，因而表示抗议。

entries.definition: serving to explain or clarify by example; it stresses understanding, while demonstrative stresses showing the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 用以举例说明的；它强调帮助理解，而 demonstrative 强调把东西本身展示出来。

entries.definition: intended to make something easier to understand; it works through words rather than through a visible display.
entries.definitionCN: 解释性的；意在让人更容易理解。它靠文字起作用，而不是靠可见的展示。

entries.definition: clearly conveying feeling or meaning; closest to the emotional sense of demonstrative, but not tied to physical affection.
entries.definitionCN: 富有表现力的；清楚传达情感或意义。它最接近 demonstrative 的情感义，但不限于身体亲昵。

entries.definition: suggesting that something is true or present; it points like a demonstrative but does not exhibit the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 表明……的；暗示某事物存在或为真。它像指示词一样指向，但不把事物展示出来。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'completely' + monstrare 'show': to demonstrate is to show something all the way through.
normal.cn: de-“完全地”+ monstrare“显示”：demonstrate 就是把东西从头到尾展示清楚。

normal.en: monstrum was an omen, something that showed itself; the modern museum label 'on display' keeps that gesture.
normal.cn: monstrum 是预兆，是自己显现出来的东西；现代展厅标签上的 on display 保留了同一个手势。

normal.en: The grammar pair is easy to remember: a demonstrative points at this or those, the way a finger points.
normal.cn: 语法搭配好记：demonstrative 指向 this 或 those，就像手指一点。

normal.en: demonstrate, demonstration, demonstrator, demonstrative all share the same stem, so learning one reinforces the rest.
normal.cn: demonstrate、demonstration、demonstrator、demonstrative 共享同一词干，学一个就强化其余。

normal.en: A demonstrative father is not showing a model; he is showing a feeling, with hugs instead of charts.
normal.cn: demonstrative 的父亲展示的不是模型，而是感情，用的是拥抱而不是图表。

abstract.en: Think of a hand lifting a glass model above a crowd, turning it slowly so every side catches the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把玻璃模型举到人群上方，慢慢转动，让每一面都反光。

abstract.en: Think of a spotlight following a single object across a stage: the light itself is the showing.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯在舞台上跟着一个物件移动：光本身就是那次“显示”。

abstract.en: Think of an open palm held out with a small object on it: nothing is hidden, and nothing needs explaining.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的手掌上放着一件小东西：没有隐藏，也无需解释。

examples.en: The museum uses demonstrative models so that visitors can touch what they are learning about.
examples.cn: 博物馆使用演示模型，让参观者能触摸他们正在了解的东西。

examples.en: In the sentence 'those apples are ripe', the word 'those' is a demonstrative.
examples.cn: 在 those apples are ripe 这句话里，those 是一个指示词。

examples.en: She was demonstrative with her students, praising them in front of the whole class.
examples.cn: 她对学生很外露，会当着全班的面表扬他们。

dict_mnemonic.text: “戴蒙strate”——戴（de）上眼镜，把蒙住的样本拿到台前（monstrate）展示 → demonstrative 演示的、感情外露的

root: 拉丁 demonstrare“完整地显示”（de- 加强 + monstrare“显示”，源自 monstrum“征兆”）；demonstrat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture: something is held out where others can see it, whether that thing is a model, a word, a proof or a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个手势：把某物举到别人看得见的地方——不管那东西是模型、词、证据还是感情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding an object up for a crowd to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把物件举起来给人群看。

branches.en: DEMONSTRATION: showing a real object or action so that one can see how it works.
branches.cn: 演示：把实物或动作摆出来，让人看见它如何运作。

branches.en: POINTING WORDS: the grammar term and its noun form keep the literal finger, turning attention into a part of speech.
branches.cn: 指示词：语法术语及其名词形式保留了字面的手指，把注意力变成一种词类。

branches.en: SHOWING FEELING: affection and public support move the display from objects to attitudes that are held out for an audience.
branches.cn: 展示情感：亲情与公开支持把展示对象从物件移到态度，态度被举出来给观众看。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND DIAGRAMS: a demonstrative exhibit and a demonstrative chart both make an invisible fact visible to the eye.
branches.cn: 证据与图表：演示性证物与说明性图表，都让看不见的事实变得可见。

branches.en: METHOD: the adjective also names the method itself, because the showing is repeated until it becomes a way of teaching.
branches.cn: 方法：这个形容词也命名方法本身，因为反复展示使它成为一种教学方式。

intro.en: Demonstrative is a Latin stem plus the English suffix -ive. The de- prefix is fossilized inside the base; only -ive is productive here, and -ly can extend it further.
intro.cn: demonstrative 是拉丁词干加英语后缀 -ive。de- 前缀已凝固在词基内部；这里只有 -ive 有能产性，-ly 还能继续扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family grows from monstrum 'omen' and monere 'warn'. Direct relatives include demonstrate, demonstration, remonstrate and monstrance; the stem appears as monstr- throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 这个拉丁词族从 monstrum“征兆”和 monere“警告”生长出来。直接同族词包括 demonstrate、demonstration、remonstrate、monstrance；词干一律作 monstr-。

items.meaning: to show clearly; to prove by showing
items.meaningCN: 演示；证明（de- 加强 + monstrare“显示”）
items.example: The engineer demonstrated the safety valve to the inspectors.
items.exampleCN: 工程师向检查员演示了安全阀。

items.meaning: a showing, a proof, or a public protest
items.meaningCN: 示范；论证；示威（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The demonstration lasted twenty minutes and ended with questions.
items.exampleCN: 演示持续了二十分钟，最后以提问结束。

items.meaning: a person who shows or protests
items.meaningCN: 示范者；示威者（-or 构成施事者名词）
items.example: Each demonstrator held a small sample of the new material.
items.exampleCN: 每位示范者手里都拿着一小块新材料样品。

items.meaning: in an openly showing manner
items.meaningCN: 外露地；示范地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: He demonstratively opened the box so everyone could see inside.
items.exampleCN: 他当众打开盒子，让大家都看见里面。

items.meaning: the quality of showing feelings openly
items.meaningCN: 感情外露的性质（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: Her demonstrativeness made the interview warmer than expected.
items.exampleCN: 她的外露让采访比预想的更温暖。

items.meaning: to show something back, hence to protest
items.meaningCN: 抗议；反对（re-“向后”+ monstrare“显示”，把不满怼回去）
items.example: The residents remonstrated with the council over the new road.
items.exampleCN: 居民就新公路一事向市政会提出抗议。

items.meaning: a vessel in which the host is shown
items.meaningCN: 圣体光座（展示圣体的器具，-ance 构成事物名词）
items.example: The monstrance is carried through the church so the host can be seen.
items.exampleCN: 圣体光座被抬着穿过教堂，让人看见圣体。

items.meaning: capable of being shown or proved
items.meaningCN: 可证明的；可演示的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The effect was demonstrable within a single lesson.
items.exampleCN: 这种效果在一节课内就能得到验证。

definition_en: the degree to which matter, people or information is packed into a given space or volume
core_image: 同一只玻璃盒里挤满小球，盒子没变大，球却越塞越多
scene: The density of the new alloy is low enough for aircraft panels but high enough to resist bending.
sceneCN: 这里 density 是「密度」（第 1 个义项：单位体积内的质量）；句意：这种新合金的密度低到可以做飞机蒙皮，又高到足以抗弯。图中可辨识物件：金属样块、天平、量筒、机翼蒙皮剖面。

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: density（作物理量时通常不可数）

senses.title: Mass packed into a volume
senses.titleCN: 密度：单位体积里装了多少质量
senses.definition: the mass of a substance per unit volume
senses.definitionCN: 某种物质单位体积所含的质量
senses.example: Iron has a higher density than aluminium, so the same block feels much heavier.
senses.exampleCN: 铁的密度比铝高，所以同样大小的块摸起来重得多。
senses.why: densus meant 'thick, close-packed'. The suffix -ity names a measurable state, so density is literally the state of being close-packed, expressed as mass divided by volume.
senses.whyCN: densus 意为“稠密、挤紧”。-ity 命名一种可测量的状态，因此 density 字面就是“被挤紧的状态”，用质量除以体积来表达。

senses.title: People per unit of land
senses.titleCN: 人口密度：一块地上住了多少人
senses.definition: the number of people living in a given area, usually per square kilometre or mile
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域内居住的人数，通常按每平方公里或每平方英里计
senses.example: The coastal plain has a population density five times that of the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海平原的人口密度是山区的五倍。
senses.why: The same 'packed in' image applies to people: densus describes a crowd standing close together, and -ity turns that closeness into a figure.
senses.whyCN: 同样的“挤在里面”意象也适用于人：densus 描述人群站得很近，-ity 把这种紧密变成数字。

senses.title: Close spacing of parts
senses.titleCN: 稠密：枝叶挨着枝叶
senses.definition: the quality of being closely spaced or thickly grown together
senses.definitionCN: 排列紧密或生长茂密、彼此挨在一起的特性
senses.example: The density of the canopy blocked almost all sunlight from the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 树冠的稠密几乎挡住了所有照进林地的阳光。
senses.why: Here the noun names a physical texture rather than a ratio. densus already contains the picture of things pressed together, so no formula is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的名词命名的是物理质地而不是比值。densus 本身就含有“东西被压在一起”的画面，因此不需要公式。

senses.title: Information packed into text
senses.titleCN: 信息密度：一句话里塞了多少内容
senses.definition: the amount of meaning or data carried by a unit of text, speech or image
senses.definitionCN: 单位文本、话语或图像所承载的意义或数据量
senses.example: The summary has a high information density, with almost no filler words.
senses.exampleCN: 这份摘要的信息密度很高，几乎没有废话。
senses.why: The metaphor treats ideas as objects that can be packed. A dense paragraph is one in which little space is wasted, echoing the original 'close-packed' sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把观点当成可以装填的物件。dense 的段落就是几乎不浪费空间，呼应了最初“挤紧”的含义。

senses.title: Optical density of film
senses.titleCN: 光学密度：底片黑到什么程度
senses.definition: the darkness of a photographic image, measured by how much light it blocks
senses.definitionCN: 摄影影像的黑暗程度，以遮挡多少光来衡量
senses.example: The printer adjusts ink density so that shadows do not turn into solid black.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机调整墨的密度，免得阴影变成死黑一片。
senses.why: In photography, particles are packed densely in the emulsion, so a dark area is literally a dense area. The technical sense keeps the physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 在摄影中，感光乳剂里的颗粒排得很密，所以暗部字面上就是 dense 的区域。这个技术义保留了物理画面。

senses.title: Buildings packed into a district
senses.titleCN: 建筑密度：同一块地上盖多少楼
senses.definition: the amount of building floor space or housing on a piece of land
senses.definitionCN: 一块土地上建筑楼面或住宅的数量
senses.example: Zoning rules limit the density of new housing near the subway station.
senses.exampleCN: 分区规划限制了地铁站附近新住宅的建筑密度。
senses.why: Urban planners measure how tightly structures are packed, reusing densus for built form. Density here is a policy number, not a physical constant.
senses.whyCN: 城市规划者衡量建筑物被塞得多紧，把 densus 用于建成形态。这里的密度是政策数字，而不是物理常数。

senses.title: Storage packed into a device
senses.titleCN: 存储密度：小芯片里装多少数据
senses.definition: the amount of data that can be stored in a given physical area or medium
senses.definitionCN: 给定物理面积或介质中可存储的数据量
senses.example: New recording methods raised the storage density of the disk by a factor of four.
senses.exampleCN: 新的记录方法把磁盘的存储密度提高了四倍。
senses.why: Data bits are treated as grains that can be packed closer. The word's core image survives the jump from atoms to bits.
senses.whyCN: 数据位被当成可以排得更紧的颗粒。这个词的核心意象从原子跳到比特后依然成立。

senses.title: Nutrient content per serving
senses.titleCN: 营养密度：一口食物里有多少营养
senses.definition: the concentration of a useful substance in a food or mixture per unit amount
senses.definitionCN: 食品或混合物中某种有用成分按单位量计算的浓度
senses.example: Legumes have a higher nutrient density than refined flour.
senses.exampleCN: 豆类的营养密度高于精制面粉。
senses.why: The sense extends 'packed in' from mass to nutritional value: the food carries many useful units in little bulk, so it is dense in nutrients.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把“装在里面”从质量扩展到营养价值：食物用很小的体积承载很多有用单位，因此营养上是 dense 的。

intro.en: Density comes from Latin densus 'thick, close-packed' plus the noun suffix -ity. The word entered English through French -ité and Latin -itas, and only later became a precise scientific ratio.
intro.cn: density 来自拉丁语 densus“稠密、挤紧”加名词后缀 -ity。这个词经法语 -ité 和拉丁语 -itas 进入英语，后来才成为精确的科学比值。

items.en: densus described anything thick, crowded or close-set, from hair and leaves to a packed crowd. Its deeper origin is uncertain; no reliable Latin relative outside this family is agreed on.
items.cn: densus 描述任何浓密、拥挤或排列紧密的东西，从毛发、树叶到密集的人群。它更早的来源不确定，标记为来源不确定，学界并未就该词族之外的可靠拉丁同族词达成一致。

items.en: The suffix -itas formed abstract nouns of state, as in densitas 'thickness'. English -ity continues this suffix through Old French -ité.
items.cn: 后缀 -itas 构成表状态的抽象名词，如 densitas“稠密”。英语 -ity 经古法语 -ité 延续了这个后缀。

items.en: Density appears in English in the 16th century, first in the general sense of closeness or thickness. The earliest exact dating is uncertain because spelling varied widely.
items.cn: density 在 16 世纪进入英语，最初是一般意义上的“紧密、浓密”。由于拼写差异很大，最早的确切年代存疑。

items.en: In the 17th century, as weighing and measuring improved, density took on the technical sense of mass per unit volume. The word shifted from a felt quality to a calculated quantity.
items.cn: 17 世纪，随着称量与测量手段改进，density 获得“单位体积质量”的技术义。这个词从可感知的性质变成了可计算的量。

items.en: Photography in the 19th century applied the term to the blackening of a negative. A dense negative blocks light strongly, so the old physical image fitted the new medium.
items.cn: 19 世纪的摄影把该词用于底片的黑化程度。dense 的底片强烈挡光，旧的物理意象正好适配新媒介。

items.en: Population, information and storage density are 20th-century extensions. Each treats people, ideas or bits as particles packed into a space, keeping densus alive as a metaphor.
items.cn: 人口密度、信息密度、存储密度是 20 世纪的引申。它们都把人口、观点或比特当作装进空间的粒子，让 densus 作为隐喻继续存活。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the densus stem; the near-meaning group shares the idea of 'how much is packed in' but measures different things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 densus 词干；近义组都含“装进去多少”的意思，但衡量的对象不同。

entries.definition: closely packed, thick, or hard to see through. It describes the state that density measures.
entries.definitionCN: 密集的；浓密的；难透过的。它描述 density 所测量的状态。

entries.definition: to make more compact or to change from gas to liquid. From con- 'together' + densus, 'pack together'.
entries.definitionCN: 压缩；浓缩；凝结。来自 con-“一起”+ densus“挤在一起”。

entries.definition: to make or become denser, especially in planning or materials science. -ify adds 'to make'.
entries.definitionCN: 使致密；提高密度，常用于规划或材料科学。-ify 表示“使……”。

entries.definition: the amount of a substance present in a unit of a mixture or solution; density can be a physical constant, while concentration depends on the mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 混合物或溶液中单位量所含某物质的量；density 可以是物理常数，而 concentration 取决于混合物。

entries.definition: the extent of something from one surface to the other; density concerns how much matter fills a volume, not how wide it is.
entries.definitionCN: 某物从一面到另一面的厚度；density 关心一个体积里装了多少物质，而不是有多宽。

entries.definition: the quality of being neatly and tightly packed; it is close to the literal densus image but has no numerical definition.
entries.definitionCN: 紧密排列的性质；它接近 densus 的字面意象，但没有数值定义。

entries.definition: the quality of not letting light through; it overlaps with photographic density but is about light transmission only.
entries.definitionCN: 不透光的性质；它与摄影密度有重叠，但只涉及光的透射。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: densus 'close-packed' + -ity 'state of': density is the state of being packed.
normal.cn: densus“挤紧”+ -ity“……的状态”：density 就是被装紧的状态。

normal.en: condense keeps the same root: con- 'together' + densus, so steam condensed into water is matter packed together.
normal.cn: condense 保留同一词根：con-“一起”+ densus，所以蒸汽凝结成水就是物质被挤到一起。

normal.en: The standard formula pairing is density = mass / volume, which is exactly 'how much in how much space'.
normal.cn: 标准公式搭配是 density = mass / volume，恰好就是“多少东西装在多大空间”。

normal.en: Population density changes with the unit chosen, so always name the area when you use it.
normal.cn: 人口密度会随所选单位变化，使用时务必说清面积单位。

normal.en: A dense forest and a dense paragraph both waste no space, which shows the same image working on two scales.
normal.cn: 茂密的森林和密实的段落都不浪费空间，这说明同一个意象在两个尺度上都成立。

abstract.en: Think of passengers pushing into a bus until the aisle disappears: the bus has not grown, but its density has.
abstract.cn: 想象乘客不断挤进公交车，直到过道消失：车没变大，密度却上去了。

abstract.en: Think of grains of sand filling a jar and the same jar feeling twice as heavy when shaken down.
abstract.cn: 想象沙粒装满罐子，摇实之后同一个罐子摸起来重了一倍。

abstract.en: Think of a single page typed with no margins, no line spacing and no wasted word: that page is information-dense.
abstract.cn: 想象一页不留边距、行距很紧、没有废话的打字稿：那一页就是信息密度高的。

examples.en: Water has a density of about one gram per cubic centimetre.
examples.cn: 水的密度约为每立方厘米一克。

examples.en: The city's population density doubled after the railway opened.
examples.cn: 铁路开通后，这座城市的人口密度翻了一倍。

examples.en: The editor cut the essay's length without lowering its density of ideas.
examples.cn: 编辑缩短了文章篇幅，却没有降低它的思想密度。

dict_mnemonic.text: “等city”——等（den）到城市（city）挤满了人，密度自然就高 → density 密度、稠密

root: 拉丁 densus“稠密、挤紧”（更早来源不确定，标为来源不确定）+ -ity“状态、性质”名词后缀（经法语 -ité 入英语）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one picture: a fixed space holding more and more units, whether those units are atoms, people, ideas, buildings or bits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一幅画：固定的空间里装进越来越多的单位——无论是原子、人、观点、建筑还是比特。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one box, more and more small balls inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只盒子，里面塞进越来越多的小球。

branches.en: PHYSICAL MEASUREMENT: photographic blackening counts how tightly matter blocks light.
branches.cn: 物理测量：底片黑化，计算物质遮挡光的程度。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND BUILDINGS: population and housing density apply the same packing figure to human settlement.
branches.cn: 人与建筑：人口密度与建筑密度把同一个装填数字用于人类聚居。

branches.en: TEXTURE AND CONTENT: a thick canopy and a nutrient-rich food both carry much in little space.
branches.cn: 质地与含量：浓密树冠与高营养食物都在小空间里承载很多。

branches.en: INFORMATION AND DATA: dense prose and dense storage pack meaning or bits into a tight medium.
branches.cn: 信息与数据：密实的文字与高密度存储，把意义或比特装进紧密的介质。

branches.en: THE RATIO ITSELF: all the other senses borrow from the calculated mass-per-volume figure as their model of 'how much in how much'.
branches.cn: 比值本身：其余义项都以“单位体积质量”这个计算式为模型，来表达“多少装在多大”。

intro.en: Density is a Latin adjective stem plus -ity. The suffix is fully productive in English; densus itself is not a living prefix or root that speakers can reuse freely.
intro.cn: density 是拉丁形容词词干加 -ity。这个后缀在英语中完全能产；densus 本身并不是说话者可自由复用的活前缀或词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin densus 'thick' yields densare 'to thicken', densitas 'thickness', and condensus 'pressed together'. The stem enters English as dens- in dense, density and condense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 densus“浓密”派生 densare“使变浓”、densitas“稠密”、condensus“压在一起的”。词干以 dens- 形式进入英语的 dense、density、condense。

items.meaning: closely packed; thick; stupid (informal)
items.meaningCN: 密集的；浓密的；（口语）愚钝的
items.example: A dense hedge ran along the entire boundary.
items.exampleCN: 一整道密实的树篱沿着边界延伸。

items.meaning: in a closely packed way
items.meaningCN: 密集地；浓密地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The valley is densely planted with rice.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷密植水稻。

items.meaning: the quality of being dense
items.meaningCN: 稠密；浓密（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The denseness of the fog delayed all flights.
items.exampleCN: 浓雾的密度让所有航班延误。

items.meaning: to make denser
items.meaningCN: 使致密；提高密度（-ify 表示“使……”）
items.example: The plan aims to densify the area around the station.
items.exampleCN: 该规划旨在提高车站周边区域的密度。

items.meaning: the state of being packed; mass per volume
items.meaningCN: 密度；稠密（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The density of the foam makes it useful for packaging.
items.exampleCN: 这种泡沫的密度使它适合做包装。

items.meaning: to pack together; to change gas to liquid
items.meaningCN: 压缩；凝结（con-“一起”+ dense“挤紧”）
items.example: Cool air causes the vapour to condense on the glass.
items.exampleCN: 冷空气使水汽在玻璃上凝结。

items.meaning: the process of packing together or condensing
items.meaningCN: 凝结；压缩（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Condensation formed inside the cold window.
items.exampleCN: 冷窗内侧形成了凝结水。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring density
items.meaningCN: 密度计（-meter 表示测量仪器）
items.example: The densimeter showed that the brine was ready.
items.exampleCN: 密度计显示盐水已经达到要求。

definition_en: the state of needing or being supported by someone or something else, or of being decided by another factor
core_image: 一根细绳把吊灯吊在天花板的钩子上，灯的全部重量都落在那个钩子上
scene: The island's dependence on imported fuel became clear when the supply ship was delayed.
sceneCN: 这里 dependence 是「依赖」（第 1 个义项：需要外部供给才能维持）；句意：补给船延误时，这座岛对外来燃料的依赖就暴露无遗。图中可辨识物件：小岛码头、空油罐、延误的补给船、等待卸货的吊车。

pos.zh: 依赖；依靠；依赖性；从属关系

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: dependence（表示状态时通常不可数）

senses.title: The state of relying on something
senses.titleCN: 依赖：重量挂在别人身上
senses.definition: the condition of needing another person or thing in order to function or survive
senses.definitionCN: 为了运作或生存而需要另一人或物的状态
senses.example: The village's dependence on the single well shaped its daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 全村对这口唯一水井的依赖塑造了它的日常生活。
senses.why: dependere means 'to hang down from'. A lamp hangs from a hook, and its weight rests on that hook; dependence is that hanging relationship turned into a state noun.
senses.whyCN: dependere 意为“悬挂于……之下”。吊灯挂在钩子上，全部重量压在钩子上；dependence 就是把这种悬挂关系变成状态名词。

senses.title: Economic reliance
senses.titleCN: 经济依赖：一条腿站着
senses.definition: a situation in which an economy needs another economy for trade, finance or supply
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体在贸易、金融或供给上需要另一经济体的状况
senses.example: The country's dependence on a single export made it fragile.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家依赖单一出口商品，因此十分脆弱。
senses.why: An economy that leans on one buyer is like a lamp with one hook. The de- prefix points downward, the direction in which support must come.
senses.whyCN: 只靠一个买家的经济体就像只有一只钩子的吊灯。de- 前缀指向下方，也就是支撑必须来自的方向。

senses.title: Drug or alcohol dependence
senses.titleCN: 药物依赖：身体已经离不开
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a person needs a substance and cannot stop without distress
senses.definitionCN: 一种医学状态，患者需要某种物质，停用即出现痛苦
senses.example: Long-term use can lead to physical dependence on the painkiller.
senses.exampleCN: 长期使用可能导致对止痛药的身体依赖。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the hanging image: the body has attached its normal function to a chemical hook. Removal of the hook produces withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了悬挂意象：身体把正常功能挂在某个化学钩子上。钩子一撤，就出现戒断反应。

senses.title: Mutual reliance
senses.titleCN: 相互依赖：两根柱子互相撑着
senses.definition: a relationship in which two parties each need the other
senses.definitionCN: 双方各自都需要对方的关系
senses.example: The two industries developed a mutual dependence that neither could easily break.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个行业发展出一种彼此都难以轻易切断的相互依赖。
senses.why: Two hanging objects can support each other, so the single hook becomes a pair of hooks. The noun still names a support relation, now symmetrical.
senses.whyCN: 两个悬挂物可以互相支撑，于是单钩变成一对钩子。这个名词仍命名支撑关系，只是现在是对称的。

senses.title: Statistical dependence
senses.titleCN: 统计依赖性：一个变量的变化牵着另一个
senses.definition: in statistics, the condition in which one variable's value is related to another's
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中一个变量的取值与另一个变量相关的状态
senses.example: The study tested the dependence of rainfall on ocean temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究检验了降雨对海洋温度的依赖性。
senses.why: A dependent variable hangs from an independent one: change the anchor and the hanging value moves. The statistical term borrows the same geometry.
senses.whyCN: 因变量悬挂在自变量上：锚点一动，悬挂的值就动。统计术语借用了同一套几何关系。

senses.title: Emotional reliance
senses.titleCN: 情感依赖：心里那根绳子
senses.definition: a psychological need for another person's approval, presence or support
senses.definitionCN: 在心理上需要他人的认可、陪伴或支持
senses.example: His emotional dependence made it hard for him to make decisions alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的情感依赖让他很难独自做决定。
senses.why: The support here is not physical weight but reassurance. The metaphor still works because the person's confidence is felt to hang from someone else.
senses.whyCN: 这里的支撑不是物理重量，而是安心感。隐喻仍然成立，因为这个人的信心被感觉成挂在别人身上。

senses.title: Technological reliance
senses.titleCN: 技术依赖：关键零件握在别人手里
senses.definition: the condition of needing foreign technology, components or expertise
senses.definitionCN: 需要外国技术、零部件或专业能力的状况
senses.example: Dependence on imported chips slowed the factory's expansion.
senses.exampleCN: 对进口芯片的依赖拖慢了工厂的扩张。
senses.why: Supply chains are chains of hooks: each stage holds the next. When a link is foreign, the whole structure leans outward.
senses.whyCN: 供应链是一串钩子：每一环吊着下一环。当某一环在海外，整个结构就向外倾斜。

senses.title: Subordinate status
senses.titleCN: 从属地位：名义上自主，实际受管
senses.definition: the status of a territory or institution that is controlled by another
senses.definitionCN: 领地或机构受另一者控制的地位
senses.example: The report described the region's long dependence on the colonial administration.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了该地区对殖民当局的长期从属。
senses.why: Political dependence is the institutional version of hanging: the smaller unit has no independent footing and takes its orders from above.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的从属是悬挂的制度版：较小单位没有独立立足点，命令来自上方。

intro.en: Dependence goes back to Latin dependere, built from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'. The literal 'hang down from' became 'rely on' in Late Latin and French, and English borrowed the state noun in the 16th century.
intro.cn: dependence 可追到拉丁 dependere，由 de-“向下”和 pendere“悬挂”构成。字面的“挂在……下面”在晚期拉丁语和法语中变成“依靠”，英语在 16 世纪借入了这个状态名词。

items.en: pendere meant 'to hang, be suspended'. It also gave pendulum and pendant, both visibly hanging objects, so the physical image is present across the family.
items.cn: pendere 意为“悬挂、被吊起”。它还派生了 pendulum 和 pendant，两者都是明显悬挂的物体，因此整个词族都带着这个物理画面。

items.en: dependere adds de- 'down from', giving 'to hang down from, be attached to'. Classical Latin used it of things physically suspended from a point.
items.cn: dependere 加 de-“从……向下”，意为“挂在……下面、附着于”。古典拉丁语用它描述实际悬挂在某个点上的东西。

items.en: The step from 'hang from' to 'rely on' is metaphorical: whatever hangs from a support cannot stand without it. Late Latin and French extend the verb to persons and conditions.
items.cn: 从“悬挂于”到“依靠”的转变是隐喻性的：挂在支撑物上的东西离开支撑就站不住。晚期拉丁语和法语把这个动词扩展到人和处境。

items.en: Dependence enters English in the 16th century as the state noun of depend. The exact first date is uncertain because dependence and dependency competed in spelling and meaning.
items.cn: dependence 在 16 世纪作为 depend 的状态名词进入英语。由于 dependence 与 dependency 在拼写和意义上长期竞争，确切的最早年代存疑。

items.en: In the 20th century, medicine standardized drug dependence for the physiological need for a substance, separating it from addiction as a broader behavioural term.
items.cn: 20 世纪，医学界用 drug dependence 固定指对某物质的生理需要，以便与范围更广的行为术语 addiction 区分。

items.en: Statistical dependence was named in the same period: variables that are not independent are said to depend on one another, keeping the anchor image.
items.cn: 统计学的“依赖性”也在同一时期得名：不独立的变量被说成彼此依赖，保留了锚点意象。

note.en: The look-alike group contains the same pend- family with different endings; the near-meaning group shares the idea of needing support but names different kinds of need.
note.cn: 形近组是同一 pend- 词族的不同词尾；近义组都含“需要支撑”的意思，但指的需要类型不同。

entries.definition: a state of reliance, a dependent territory, or a required software component. It overlaps with dependence but is more countable and more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖状态、属地，或软件依赖项。它与 dependence 重叠，但更可数、更技术化。

entries.definition: relying on another; also a person who is supported by someone else. It describes the one who hangs, not the relation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的；亦指受抚养人。它描述“悬挂者”，而不是关系本身。

entries.definition: reliable and trustworthy. The -able suffix shifts the meaning from 'needing support' to 'able to be relied on'.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的；可信赖的。-able 后缀把意义从“需要支撑”转成“可以被依靠”。

entries.definition: the state of depending on someone or something, often with trust; it stresses confidence more than structural necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的依赖，常带信任意味；它比结构性必需更强调信心。

entries.definition: a strong compulsive need for a substance or activity; broader and more behavioural than drug dependence.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物质或活动的强烈强迫性需要；比 drug dependence 范围更广，更偏行为层面。

entries.definition: mutual dependence between parties; it names the two-way version of the same hanging relation.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间的相互依赖；它命名的是同一悬挂关系的双向版本。

entries.definition: the state of being lower in rank or under another's authority; it concerns power, while dependence concerns need.
entries.definitionCN: 地位较低或受他人管辖的状态；它关乎权力，而 dependence 关乎需要。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + pendere 'hang': dependence is the state of hanging from a support.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”：dependence 就是挂在支撑物下面的状态。

normal.en: pendulum and pendant are visible cousins: they hang, and dependence names what hanging means for people.
normal.cn: pendulum 和 pendant 是看得见的同族词：它们都悬挂，而 dependence 命名“悬挂”对人意味着什么。

normal.en: The usual preposition is on, which matches the image: the lamp hangs on the hook.
normal.cn: 常用介词是 on，正好对应画面：灯挂在钩子上（hangs on the hook）。

normal.en: dependent is the adjective, dependence the state noun, dependency the countable or territorial noun; keep the endings apart.
normal.cn: dependent 是形容词，dependence 是状态名词，dependency 是可数或属地名词；词尾要分清。

normal.en: independence is the same image with the negative prefix: no hook, standing on its own.
normal.cn: independence 是同一画面加否定前缀：没有钩子，自己站住。

abstract.en: Think of a single nail holding a heavy picture frame: remove the nail and the frame falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子挂着沉重的画框：钉子一拔，画框就掉。

abstract.en: Think of a climber clipped to one rope: every move is safe only while the rope holds.
abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者只扣在一根绳上：只要绳子还牢，每个动作才安全。

abstract.en: Think of two drunks holding each other up: neither can walk alone, which is mutual dependence.
abstract.cn: 想象两个醉汉互相扶着走：谁也不能独自走，这就是相互依赖。

examples.en: Reducing dependence on imported oil became the government's main energy goal.
examples.cn: 减少对进口石油的依赖成了政府的主要能源目标。

examples.en: The doctor warned that dependence on sleeping pills can develop quickly.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，对安眠药的依赖可能很快形成。

examples.en: Their friendship rested on a healthy dependence rather than on control.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊建立在健康的依赖之上，而不是控制之上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地喷den斯”——地上（de）喷出的喷泉（pen）全靠水泵撑着 → dependence 依赖、依靠

root: 拉丁 dependere“挂在……下面、依附”（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）；depend- 词干 + -ence 状态名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one geometry: something hangs from a support, and its ability to stay in place belongs to that support.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一套几何关系：某物挂在支撑上，它能否留在原位取决于那个支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a weight hanging from a single hook.
core.cn: 核心意象：重量挂在唯一一只钩子上。

branches.en: TWO HOOKS: mutual reliance is the same hanging relation drawn with two supports.
branches.cn: 两只钩子：相互依赖是同一悬挂关系画成双支撑。

branches.en: ECONOMIC AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT: an economy leaning on one export and a factory leaning on imported chips both hang outward.
branches.cn: 经济与技术支撑：依赖单一出口的经济体和依赖进口芯片的工厂，都向外悬挂。

branches.en: BODY AND MIND: chemical dependence and emotional dependence attach normal functioning to a hook outside the self.
branches.cn: 身体与心理：药物依赖与情感依赖都把正常运转挂到自我之外的钩子上。

branches.en: STATISTICS AND POLITICS: a dependent variable and a dependent territory both take their position from a stronger anchor.
branches.cn: 统计与政治：因变量与属地都从更强的锚点那里取得自己的位置。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every extension keeps the original 'hanging' meaning and adds only the kind of support involved.
branches.cn: 基础义：每个引申都保留最初的“悬挂”含义，只增加所涉及的支撑类型。

intro.en: Dependence is depend plus -ence, a Latin-derived state suffix. Both de- and pendere are fossilized inside the base; English adds only -ence, and -ent or -ency for related forms.
intro.cn: dependence 是 depend 加 -ence（源自拉丁的状态后缀）。de- 与 pendere 都已凝固在词基内；英语只加 -ence，相关形式则用 -ent 或 -ency。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere 'to hang' yields pendulus 'hanging', dependere 'hang from', and the noun dependens. The stem pend- also appears in pendulum, pendant and suspend.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pendere“悬挂”派生 pendulus“悬挂的”、dependere“挂在……下”以及名词 dependens。词干 pend- 也出现在 pendulum、pendant、suspend 中。

items.meaning: to hang from; to rely on
items.meaningCN: 悬挂于；依赖；取决于（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）
items.example: The harvest depends on how much rain falls in spring.
items.exampleCN: 收成取决于春季降雨量。

items.meaning: relying on another; supported by another
items.meaningCN: 依赖的；受抚养的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: A dependent child must be listed on the form.
items.exampleCN: 受抚养子女必须填在表格上。

items.meaning: the state of relying on something
items.meaningCN: 依赖；依靠（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Dependence on a single supplier is a business risk.
items.exampleCN: 依赖单一供应商是一种商业风险。

items.meaning: reliance; a dependent territory; a required component
items.meaningCN: 依赖；属地；依赖项（-ency 构成状态或事物名词）
items.example: The software update broke an old dependency.
items.exampleCN: 这次软件更新破坏了一个旧的依赖项。

items.meaning: able to be relied on
items.meaningCN: 可靠的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The old generator is noisy but dependable.
items.exampleCN: 那台旧发电机很吵，但很可靠。

items.meaning: in a reliable way
items.meaningCN: 可靠地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The bus arrives dependably at seven each morning.
items.exampleCN: 这趟公交每天早上七点准点到。

items.meaning: not relying on another
items.meaningCN: 独立的；不受支配的（in-“不”+ dependent）
items.example: The laboratory is independent of the manufacturer.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室独立于制造商。

items.meaning: mutual reliance
items.meaningCN: 相互依赖（inter-“之间”+ dependence）
items.example: Global trade rests on a web of interdependence.
items.exampleCN: 全球贸易建立在一张相互依赖的网上。

latinEntries.meaning: to hang down from; to be attached to

definition_zh: 依赖的；受抚养的；取决于……的；从属的
definition_en: needing another person or thing for support, or decided by a particular condition
core_image: 一个孩子紧紧拽着大人的衣角过马路
scene: The final result is dependent on whether the second sample was stored correctly.
sceneCN: 这里 dependent 是「取决于……的」（第 2 个义项：由某条件决定）；句意：最终结果取决于第二个样本是否被正确保存。图中可辨识物件：两个样本瓶、标签、温度记录仪、结果表格。

pos.zh: 依赖的；受抚养的；取决于……的；从属的

senses.title: Needing support to function
senses.titleCN: 依赖的：自己撑不住
senses.definition: unable to manage without the help or presence of another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 没有另一人或物的帮助或存在便无法应付的
senses.example: After the operation she was dependent on her sister for everyday tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后，她日常起居都依赖姐姐。
senses.why: dependere means 'to hang from'. A dependent person is suspended from a support: the weight is real, and removing the support would bring the person down.
senses.whyCN: dependere 意为“悬挂于”。dependent 的人被吊在某个支撑上：重量是真实的，撤掉支撑人就会落下。

senses.title: Decided by a condition
senses.titleCN: 取决于……的：条件一动，结果就动
senses.definition: controlled or determined by another factor
senses.definitionCN: 受另一因素控制或决定的
senses.example: The crop yield is dependent on the amount of rain in June.
senses.exampleCN: 作物产量取决于六月的降雨量。
senses.why: In this sense the support is a condition rather than a person. The outcome hangs from the condition, so change the condition and the outcome swings.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项里的支撑是条件而不是人。结果挂在条件上，条件一变，结果就摆动。

senses.title: Financially supported
senses.titleCN: 经济上依赖的：账单一来就得找人
senses.definition: relying on another person's income or money
senses.definitionCN: 依靠他人收入或金钱的
senses.example: He remained financially dependent on his parents until his late twenties.
senses.exampleCN: 他直到快三十岁在经济上还依赖父母。
senses.why: Money is the hook here. The person's living costs hang from another budget, which is the economic version of the original suspension image.
senses.whyCN: 这里的钩子是钱。这个人的生活开支挂在另一份预算上，这就是原始悬挂意象的经济版。

senses.title: A person who is supported
senses.titleCN: 名词：受抚养的人
senses.definition: a person, especially a child or relative, who is supported by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 由他人抚养或供养的人，尤指子女或亲属
senses.example: The tax form asks how many dependents live in the household.
senses.exampleCN: 税表要求填写家中有几名受抚养人。
senses.why: As a noun, dependent names the hanging object itself rather than the relation. The -ent ending marks the person who receives the support.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，dependent 命名的是悬挂物本身，而不是关系。-ent 词尾标记接受支撑的人。

senses.title: The variable that responds
senses.titleCN: 因变量：被牵动的那个数
senses.definition: in an experiment, the variable whose value is measured and expected to change in response to another variable
senses.definitionCN: 实验中其取值被测量、并预期随另一变量变化的变量
senses.example: Reaction time was the dependent variable in the sleep study.
senses.exampleCN: 反应时是这项睡眠研究中的因变量。
senses.why: The dependent variable hangs from the independent one: the researcher changes the anchor and watches what swings. The grammar of the phrase mirrors the physics.
senses.whyCN: 因变量挂在自变量上：研究者改变锚点，观察什么在摆动。这个短语的语法映射了这套物理关系。

senses.title: Grammar: unable to stand alone
senses.titleCN: 从句：离开主句就站不住
senses.definition: in grammar, describing a clause that cannot form a sentence by itself
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指不能独立成句的分句
senses.example: In 'because it rained', the dependent clause needs a main clause to complete the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 在 because it rained 中，这个从句需要主句才能构成完整句子。
senses.why: A dependent clause leans on a main clause for its grammatical footing, exactly as a hanging object leans on a hook. The term borrows the same support metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 从句靠主句获得语法立足点，正如悬挂物靠钩子。这个术语借用了同一个支撑隐喻。

senses.title: Medically reliant on a substance
senses.titleCN: 药物依赖的：身体离不开它
senses.definition: physiologically needing a drug or substance to function normally
senses.definitionCN: 生理上需要某种药物或物质才能正常运作的
senses.example: Some patients become dependent on painkillers after long treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 有些病人在长期治疗后会对止痛药产生依赖。
senses.why: The body has attached its normal chemistry to the drug. The adjective describes that attachment, not a moral failing, which is why medical writing prefers it to 'addicted'.
senses.whyCN: 身体把正常化学状态挂在这种药上。这个形容词描述的是这种附着，而不是道德缺陷，因此医学写作更偏好它而非 addicted。

senses.title: Politically subordinate
senses.titleCN: 从属的：名义自主、实际受管
senses.definition: controlled by another state or authority
senses.definitionCN: 受另一国家或当局控制的
senses.example: The island was a dependent territory for most of the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 该岛在上个世纪的大部分时间里是一块属地。
senses.why: A dependent territory has no independent footing; its administration hangs from a larger government, which is the institutional reading of pendere.
senses.whyCN: 属地没有独立立足点，其行政挂在更大的政府上；这是 pendere 的制度化读法。

intro.en: Dependent is the adjective from Latin dependere 'to hang from', de- 'down' plus pendere 'to hang'. English took the adjective from French in the 15th century; the noun use for a supported person followed later.
intro.cn: dependent 是拉丁 dependere“挂在……下”的形容词，由 de-“向下”与 pendere“悬挂”构成。英语在 15 世纪从法语借入该形容词，后来才把它用作“受抚养人”的名词。

items.en: pendere 'to hang' is also the source of pendulum and pendant. The root is visible in every member: something is suspended and moves only as the support allows.
items.cn: pendere“悬挂”也是 pendulum 和 pendant 的来源。词根在每个成员身上都可见：某物被吊起，只能随支撑允许的方式移动。

items.en: dependere 'to hang down from, be attached to' adds de- 'down'. Classical Latin used it for physical suspension; the figurative 'rely on' grows in later Latin.
items.cn: dependere“挂在……下面、附着”加了 de-“向下”。古典拉丁语用它表示实际悬挂；比喻义的“依靠”在晚期拉丁语中发展起来。

items.en: French dépendant supplied the English adjective in the 15th century. The -ant ending was later reshaped to -ent by association with Latin participles.
items.cn: 法语 dépendant 在 15 世纪提供了英语形容词。后来受拉丁分词联想影响，-ant 词尾被改写为 -ent。

items.en: From the 16th to 18th century, dependent also became a noun for a person who relies on another. The exact first date of this noun use is uncertain.
items.cn: 16 至 18 世纪，dependent 又成为名词，指依赖他人的人。这一名词用法的最早确切年代存疑。

items.en: Grammar adopted dependent clause and statistics adopted dependent variable in the 19th and 20th centuries, both extending the support metaphor to structure and data.
items.cn: 语法在 19 至 20 世纪采用 dependent clause，统计学采用 dependent variable，两者都把支撑隐喻扩展到结构和数据。

items.en: Modern medicine uses dependent for physiological reliance on a drug. The phrasing keeps the word descriptive rather than judgmental, unlike 'addicted'.
items.cn: 现代医学用 dependent 表示对药物的生理依赖。这种说法保持描述性而非评判性，与 addicted 不同。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts the -ent, -ence and -able forms of one family; the near-meaning group separates kinds of reliance that English keeps distinct.
note.cn: 形近组对比同一词族的 -ent、-ence、-able 形式；近义组区分英语中保持不同的几种“依赖”。

entries.definition: reliable, able to be depended on. The -able suffix reverses the direction: this person supports others.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的，可以被依赖的。-able 后缀反转了方向：这个人是支撑别人的人。

entries.definition: the state of relying on someone or something; it names the relation, while dependent names the relying party.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖他人或某物的状态；它命名关系，而 dependent 命名依赖的一方。

entries.definition: a person supported by another. The spelling is identical to the adjective; only the grammatical slot tells you which is meant.
entries.definitionCN: 受他人抚养的人。拼写与形容词完全相同，只能靠语法位置判断是哪一个。

entries.definition: depending on someone with trust; it foregrounds confidence, while dependent foregrounds need.
entries.definitionCN: 带着信任依赖某人；它突出信心，而 dependent 突出需要。

entries.definition: depending on a condition being met; close to 'dependent on' but usual of agreements and offers rather than causal relations.
entries.definitionCN: 以某条件得到满足为前提的；接近 dependent on，但更常用于协议和提议，而非因果关系。

entries.definition: lower in rank or importance; it concerns hierarchy, whereas dependent concerns support.
entries.definitionCN: 级别或重要性较低的；它关乎等级，而 dependent 关乎支撑。

entries.definition: unable to stop using a substance or doing something; it adds compulsion to dependence and carries a stronger judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 无法停止使用某物或做某事；它在依赖之上加了强迫性，并带有更强的评判色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + pendere 'hang': a dependent thing hangs down from its support.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”：dependent 的东西挂在支撑下方。

normal.en: The fixed phrase dependent on keeps the preposition that matches the picture: hanging on a hook.
normal.cn: 固定短语 dependent on 保留了与画面一致的介词：挂在钩子上。

normal.en: dependent, dependence, dependency, depend all share pend-; learn the noun endings as a set.
normal.cn: dependent、dependence、dependency、depend 共享 pend-；把名词词尾当一组来记。

normal.en: In an experiment, change the independent variable and watch the dependent variable respond.
normal.cn: 在实验中，改变自变量，观察因变量如何响应。

normal.en: A dependent clause is the grammatical cousin of a dependent child: both need a stronger partner to stand.
normal.cn: dependent clause 是 dependent child 的语法表亲：两者都需要更强的搭档才能站住。

abstract.en: Think of a small boat tied to a pier: it can float, but it cannot leave the rope.
abstract.cn: 想象一只系在码头的小船：它能漂，但离不开那根绳。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp plugged into one socket: the light is bright only while the socket supplies power.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏插在唯一插座上的灯：只有插座供电时它才亮。

abstract.en: Think of a plant growing on a trellis: without the frame it would fall flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一株攀在棚架上的植物：没有架子它就会倒伏。

examples.en: The project's success is dependent on cooperation between the two teams.
examples.cn: 项目的成功取决于两个团队之间的合作。

examples.en: As a dependent, she qualifies for the family medical plan.
examples.cn: 作为受抚养人，她符合家庭医疗计划的资格。

examples.en: In the experiment, temperature was the independent variable and growth the dependent one.
examples.cn: 实验中，温度是自变量，生长量是因变量。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地喷等”——地上（de）喷出的水柱等着（pend）下面的桶来接 → dependent 依赖的、取决于的

root: 拉丁 dependere“挂在……下面、依附”（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）；depend- 词干 + -ent 形容词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one posture: something leans on a support above it, and what it can do is limited by that support.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个姿态：某物靠在它上方的支撑上，它能做什么由那个支撑限定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child holding the edge of an adult's coat while crossing.
core.cn: 核心意象：过马路时孩子紧紧拽着大人的衣角。

branches.en: FINANCIAL SUPPORT: the bill arrives and one must turn to someone else.
branches.cn: 经济支撑：账单一来就得找人。

branches.en: CONDITIONS AND VARIABLES: a yield controlled by rain and a value controlled by an input both swing from an anchor they do not own.
branches.cn: 条件与变量：受降雨控制的产量与受输入控制的值，都从并非自己所有的锚点摆动。

branches.en: PERSON AND BODY: a supported person and a body needing a drug are two readings of the same reliance, one social and one chemical.
branches.cn: 人与身体：受抚养的人与需要药物的身体，是同一依赖的两种读法，一为社会性，一为化学性。

branches.en: GRAMMAR AND POLITICS: a dependent clause and a dependent territory both lack independent footing.
branches.cn: 语法与政治：从句与属地都缺少独立立足点。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every other sense specifies what kind of support is being held onto.
branches.cn: 基础义：其余义项都只是说明抓住的是哪一种支撑。

intro.en: Dependent is depend plus -ent, the Latin adjective ending. The de- and pendere parts are not separable in English, so only -ent and the related -ence, -ency, -able endings are productive.
intro.cn: dependent 是 depend 加 -ent（拉丁形容词词尾）。de- 与 pendere 在英语中不可分割，因此只有 -ent 及相关的 -ence、-ency、-able 词尾有能产性。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere 'hang' gives dependere, dependens and pendulus. English relatives include depend, dependence, dependency, pendulum and suspend, all carrying a suspended object.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pendere“悬挂”派生 dependere、dependens、pendulus。英语同族词包括 depend、dependence、dependency、pendulum、suspend，都带有一个被吊起的物体。

items.meaning: to rely on; to be decided by
items.meaningCN: 依赖；取决于（de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”）
items.example: Everything depends on the weather tomorrow.
items.exampleCN: 一切都取决于明天的天气。

items.meaning: the state of relying on another
items.meaningCN: 依赖状态（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: The policy aims to reduce dependence on foreign fuel.
items.exampleCN: 该政策旨在减少对外国燃料的依赖。

items.meaning: reliance; a dependent territory; a required component
items.meaningCN: 依赖；属地；依赖项（-ency 构成状态或事物名词）
items.example: The old library is no longer a dependency of the project.
items.exampleCN: 那个旧库已不再是该项目的依赖项。

items.meaning: relying on another; conditional on another
items.meaningCN: 依赖的；取决于……的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: The plan is dependent on approval from the board.
items.exampleCN: 该计划取决于董事会的批准。

items.meaning: in a dependent manner
items.meaningCN: 依赖地；从属地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The two species evolved dependently within the same habitat.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种在同一栖息地内相互依赖地演化。

items.meaning: able to be relied on
items.meaningCN: 可靠的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: She is the most dependable member of the team.
items.exampleCN: 她是团队里最可靠的成员。

items.meaning: not relying on another
items.meaningCN: 独立的（in-“不”+ dependent）
items.example: The study was independent of industry funding.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究独立于行业资助。

items.meaning: relying on each other
items.meaningCN: 相互依赖的（inter-“之间”+ dependent）
items.example: Modern supply chains are deeply interdependent.
items.exampleCN: 现代供应链高度相互依赖。

latinEntries.meaning: to hang from; to be attached

definition_zh: 部署；调配；展开；投入使用
definition_en: the act of moving people, equipment or software into position and putting them into use
core_image: 一队士兵从行军队形展开，铺满整条防线
scene: The deployment of rescue teams began within an hour of the earthquake.
sceneCN: 这里 deployment 是「部署、调配」（第 2 个义项：把应急力量派到位置并投入使用）；句意：地震后一小时内，救援队的部署就开始了。图中可辨识物件：救援车、帐篷、担架、地图上标出的集结点。

pos.zh: 部署；调配；展开；投入使用

senses.title: Moving troops into position
senses.titleCN: 军事部署：把部队摆到该在的位置
senses.definition: the movement of military forces into the positions where they will operate
senses.definitionCN: 把军事力量调动到其将执行任务的位置
senses.example: The deployment of two brigades to the border took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 两个旅部署到边境花了三天。
senses.why: deploy comes from 'to unfold'. Troops folded into columns are unfolded across a front, so deployment is literally the spreading out of a force.
senses.whyCN: deploy 本义是“展开”。折成纵队的部队被展开到整条正面，因此 deployment 字面上就是兵力的铺开。

senses.title: Sending emergency teams
senses.titleCN: 应急力量部署：把人派到现场
senses.definition: the dispatch of police, medical or rescue units to an incident
senses.definitionCN: 把警察、医疗或救援单位派往事件现场
senses.example: Rapid deployment of medical staff saved several injured passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 医护人员的快速部署救下了几名受伤乘客。
senses.why: The same unfolding happens on a smaller scale: folded units are spread across a site. The word does not require an army, only a force that must occupy ground.
senses.whyCN: 同样的展开发生在更小的尺度：成建制的单位被铺到一个现场。这个词不要求军队，只要求一支必须占据地面的力量。

senses.title: Allocating people and equipment
senses.titleCN: 资源调配：把人和设备放到需要处
senses.definition: the organized assignment of staff, money or equipment to tasks
senses.definitionCN: 把人员、资金或设备有组织地分配到任务上
senses.example: The deployment of engineers to the northern site slowed the southern work.
senses.exampleCN: 把工程师调往北部工地拖慢了南部的进度。
senses.why: Deployment implies a map: resources are folded up in one place and unfolded where needed. Allocation is the civilian version of the same operation.
senses.whyCN: deployment 隐含着地图：资源在一处被收拢，在需要处被展开。分配就是同一操作的民用版。

senses.title: Releasing software into service
senses.titleCN: 软件部署：把程序装到每台机器
senses.definition: the process of installing, configuring and activating software across systems
senses.definitionCN: 在各系统上安装、配置并启用软件的过程
senses.example: The deployment of the new scheduling system caused a day of confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 新排班系统的部署造成了一天的混乱。
senses.why: Code stored in a repository is folded away; deployment unfolds it onto many machines. The metaphor fits because the software is spread out where it will run.
senses.whyCN: 仓库里的代码是折起来收着的；部署把它展开到许多机器上。这个隐喻贴切，因为软件被铺到它要运行的地方。

senses.title: Putting arguments into play
senses.titleCN: 话术的运用：把论点摆上桌
senses.definition: the strategic use of words, skills or arguments to achieve an effect
senses.definitionCN: 为达到某种效果而策略性地使用言辞、技能或论点
senses.example: The report criticized the deployment of fear rather than evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 报告批评了用恐惧而不是证据来做说服。
senses.why: Rhetorical deployment treats arguments as troops: they are placed where they can do the most work. The military image is borrowed deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 修辞上的 deployment 把论点当成部队：把它们摆到最能发挥作用的位置。这里有意借用了军事意象。

senses.title: Unfolding something physically
senses.titleCN: 展开：把折起的东西铺开
senses.definition: the act of opening out or extending something that was folded
senses.definitionCN: 把折叠之物打开或伸展的动作
senses.example: The deployment of the solar wings took several minutes after launch.
senses.exampleCN: 发射后，太阳能翼的展开花了几分钟。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal sense. Modern French déployer still means 'to unfold', and English keeps that physical meaning in space and engineering writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最字面的义项。现代法语 déployer 仍表示“展开”，英语在航天与工程写作中保留了这一物理义。

senses.title: A fleet's operational tour
senses.titleCN: 舰队部署：一整轮海外执勤
senses.definition: the period during which a naval force operates away from its home base
senses.definitionCN: 海军力量离开母港在外执行任务的那段时间
senses.example: The carrier returned home after a seven-month deployment.
senses.exampleCN: 航母在为期七个月的部署后返回母港。
senses.why: A fleet spread across foreign waters is a deployed force. The noun shifts from the act of moving to the whole period of being spread out.
senses.whyCN: 散布在海外海域的舰队就是被部署的力量。这个名词从“调动的动作”转指“被铺开的整个时期”。

senses.title: Putting capital to work
senses.titleCN: 资金投放：把钱铺到项目上
senses.definition: the investment of funds or assets into projects expected to produce returns
senses.definitionCN: 把资金或资产投入预期产生回报的项目
senses.example: The fund's deployment into green energy reached two billion dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金投入绿色能源的资金达到二十亿美元。
senses.why: Capital held in reserve is folded up; once invested it is spread across projects. Finance borrowed the military word because both involve placing assets where they can act.
senses.whyCN: 留存的资本是折起来的；一旦投资就被铺到各个项目。金融借用这个军事词，因为两者都涉及把资产放到能发挥作用的位置。

intro.en: Deployment is the noun of deploy, borrowed from French déployer 'to unfold'. French traces it to Latin displicare, dis- 'apart' plus plicare 'to fold'. The military sense dominates English usage, and the software sense is recent.
intro.cn: deployment 是 deploy 的名词，借自法语 déployer“展开”。法语可追到拉丁 displicare，由 dis-“分开”和 plicare“折叠”构成。军事义主导了英语用法，软件义则是晚近才出现的。

items.en: plicare meant 'to fold, bend, twist'. A folded thing occupies less ground, so unfolding it is the act of spreading it across space.
items.cn: plicare 意为“折叠、弯、扭”。折起的东西占的地方小，把它打开就是让它铺满空间。

items.en: displicare adds dis- 'apart' to plicare, giving 'to unfold, spread out'. This Latin verb is also the ancestor of English display, a close doublet of deploy.
items.cn: displicare 给 plicare 加 dis-“分开”，意为“展开、铺开”。这个拉丁动词也是英语 display 的祖先，display 与 deploy 是一对近双式词。

items.en: Old French desplier became modern déployer, still the ordinary verb for unfolding a map or a sail. English borrowed the military form deploy in the 15th to 17th century; exact dating is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 desplier 演变为现代 déployer，至今仍是“展开地图或帆”的常用动词。英语在 15 至 17 世纪借入军事形式的 deploy，确切年代存疑。

items.en: By the 17th century deploy was a technical term for extending a body of troops from column into line. Deployment names that manoeuvre and, by extension, any placing of forces.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，deploy 已是把部队从纵队展开成横队的技术术语。deployment 命名这一机动，并引申指任何力量布置。

items.en: In the 20th century the word spread to police, rescue, equipment and resources. The common thread is still movement into position followed by use.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到警察、救援、设备和资源。共同线索仍是“进入位置后再投入使用”。

items.en: Software deployment appears in the late 20th century. Code is stored folded in a repository and unfolded onto servers, so the old metaphor survived the change of material.
items.cn: 软件部署出现于 20 世纪后期。代码折叠存放在仓库里，再展开到服务器上，因此旧隐喻在材料改变后依然存活。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the plicare root through different prefixes; the near-meaning group shares the idea of placing something where it can work.
note.cn: 形近组经不同前缀共享 plicare 词根；近义组都含“把某物放到能发挥作用之处”的意思。

entries.definition: to move forces or resources into position; to unfold. Deployment is the noun of this action.
entries.definitionCN: 把力量或资源调到位；展开。deployment 是这一动作的名词。

entries.definition: to deploy again or move to a new position. re- 'again' marks a second unfolding.
entries.definitionCN: 重新部署或调往新位置。re-“再次”标记第二次展开。

entries.tag: doublet from the same Latin verb
entries.definition: to arrange something so it can be seen. It comes from the same displicare but stresses visibility rather than operational placement.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物摆出来给人看。它来自同一个 displicare，但强调可见性，而非作战位置。

entries.definition: the act of putting something in a particular place; it is neutral about whether the thing is then used.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置；它对之后是否投入使用不加说明。

entries.definition: the act of preparing and assembling forces for action; it stresses readiness rather than final placement.
entries.definitionCN: 为行动准备并集结力量；它强调准备就绪，而非最终位置。

entries.definition: the act of fixing equipment or software in place so it can work; common for software, but narrower than deployment.
entries.definitionCN: 把设备或软件装到位使其可运行；软件语境常用，但比 deployment 窄。

entries.definition: the assignment of resources to users or tasks; it concerns shares, while deployment concerns placement and use.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源分配给使用者或任务；它关注份额，而 deployment 关注位置与使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'apart' + plicare 'fold': to deploy is to unfold a force across the ground.
normal.cn: de-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”：deploy 就是把力量在地面上展开。

normal.en: display is a doublet: same Latin verb, but display is about being seen, deploy about being placed.
normal.cn: display 是同源双式词：同一个拉丁动词，但 display 讲被看见，deploy 讲被放置。

normal.en: The standard pairing is troop deployment; if you can say 'troops', you are in the military sense.
normal.cn: 标准搭配是 troop deployment；如果能接 troops，你就在军事义里。

normal.en: Software deployment keeps the same logic: code folded in a repository is unfolded onto servers.
normal.cn: 软件部署保持同一逻辑：仓库里折起的代码被展开到服务器上。

normal.en: redeployment is the same map drawn twice: units are folded up and unfolded somewhere else.
normal.cn: redeployment 是同一张地图画两次：单位被收拢，再在别处展开。

abstract.en: Think of a paper map folded into a pocket and then opened across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图折起来塞进口袋，再在桌面上整幅展开。

abstract.en: Think of a fan closed in a hand and then spread until every rib shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一把扇子收在手里，再展开到每根扇骨都露出。

abstract.en: Think of chess pieces lifted from a box and placed on every relevant square before play begins.
abstract.cn: 想象棋子在开局前从盒子里取出，摆到每一个相关格子。

examples.en: The deployment of additional nurses reduced waiting times in the emergency room.
examples.cn: 增派护士的部署缩短了急诊室的等候时间。

examples.en: The company delayed the deployment of the update until the weekend.
examples.cn: 公司把更新的部署推迟到周末。

examples.en: Critics questioned the deployment of public money into a risky venture.
examples.cn: 批评者质疑把公共资金投入高风险项目的做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地铺罗伊”——地上（de）铺（ploy）开洛伊的部队，一排排站好 → deployment 部署、展开

root: 法语 déployer“展开” ← 古法语 desplier ← 拉丁 displicare“展开”（dis-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”）；deploy + -ment 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one motion: something folded or held in reserve is opened out and placed where it can act.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：收着或折着的东西被打开，放到能发挥作用的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: troops unfolding from column into a line across the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：部队从纵队展开成横贯正面的横队。

branches.en: THE TOUR: a fleet’s time abroad is the same deployment seen across a span of time.
branches.cn: 舰队部署：一整轮海外执勤，是同一部署在时间跨度上的看法。

branches.en: CIVILIAN FORCES AND RESOURCES: rescue teams and engineers are deployed exactly as troops are, by placing them where the need is.
branches.cn: 民用力量与资源：救援队与工程师的部署方式与部队相同，都是放到需要之处。

branches.en: SOFTWARE AND PHYSICAL UNFOLDING: code spread onto servers and a solar wing opening in orbit both repeat the literal unfolding.
branches.cn: 软件与物理展开：代码铺到服务器、太阳能翼在轨道打开，都重复了字面意义上的展开。

branches.en: ARGUMENTS AND CAPITAL: rhetoric and money are placed like forces, each deployed where it can produce the greatest effect.
branches.cn: 论点与资本：话术和金钱都像力量一样被放置，各自部署到最能产生效果的地方。

branches.en: THE BASE IMAGE: all extensions keep the idea of an organised body moving from storage into operational space.
branches.cn: 基础意象：所有引申都保留“有组织的整体从储备状态进入运作空间”的观念。

intro.en: Deployment is deploy plus -ment, a noun suffix of action or result. The Latin prefix and root are fused inside deploy; English productively adds re- and -able around it.
intro.cn: deployment 是 deploy 加 -ment（表动作或结果的名词后缀）。拉丁前缀与词根已融合在 deploy 内部；英语在它外面能产地加 re- 和 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' yields displicare 'unfold', explicare 'unfold, explain', implicare 'fold in', and replicare 'fold back'. English receives branches through French: deploy, display, exploit, employ.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare“折叠”派生 displicare“展开”、explicare“展开、解释”、implicare“折进去”、replicare“折回”。英语经法语接收了各分支：deploy、display、exploit、employ。

items.meaning: to unfold; to move into position
items.meaningCN: 展开；部署（dis-“分开”+ plicare“折叠”）
items.example: The unit was deployed along the eastern ridge.
items.exampleCN: 该部队被部署在东侧山脊沿线。

items.meaning: the act or result of deploying
items.meaningCN: 部署；展开（-ment 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The deployment of the field hospital took a full day.
items.exampleCN: 野战医院的部署花了一整天。

items.meaning: to deploy again or elsewhere
items.meaningCN: 重新部署；调往别处（re-“再次”+ deploy）
items.example: Half the staff were redeployed to the new branch.
items.exampleCN: 一半员工被重新部署到新分公司。

items.meaning: a second or new deployment
items.meaningCN: 重新部署（re- + deploy + -ment）
items.example: Redeployment of the team followed the plant closure.
items.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后团队被重新部署。

items.meaning: capable of being deployed
items.meaningCN: 可部署的；可展开的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The reserve unit is deployable within twelve hours.
items.exampleCN: 预备役部队可在十二小时内完成部署。

items.meaning: to unfold for viewing
items.meaningCN: 展示；陈列（同源双式词，强调被看见）
items.example: The samples were displayed on a long table.
items.exampleCN: 样品陈列在一张长桌上。

items.meaning: to unfold; to make full use of
items.meaningCN: 开发；利用（ex-“向外”+ plicare“折叠”，把潜力展开）
items.example: The company exploited a gap in the market.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司利用了一个市场空白。

items.meaning: to fold in; to use or hire
items.meaningCN: 雇用；使用（由“折进去、纳入其中”引申）
items.example: The lab employs forty researchers.
items.exampleCN: 这家实验室雇用了四十名研究员。

definition_zh: 沉积；沉积物；宣誓证词；罢免
definition_en: the laying down of material; the material laid down; sworn testimony; or removal from power
core_image: 河水放慢，沙粒一层层落在河底
scene: The deposition of fine silt each spring keeps the delta fertile.
sceneCN: 这里 deposition 是「沉积作用」（第 1 个义项：物质被放下并堆积）；句意：每年春天细淤泥的沉积让三角洲保持肥沃。图中可辨识物件：河湾、缓流、沉降的细沙、层层叠起的河岸剖面。

pos.zh: 沉积；沉积物；宣誓证词；罢免

senses.title: Sediment laid down by water or wind
senses.titleCN: 沉积作用：颗粒一层层落下来
senses.definition: the geological process by which loose material settles out of water, wind or ice
senses.definitionCN: 松散物质从水、风或冰中沉降并堆积的地质过程
senses.example: Deposition of sand at the river mouth slowly built a new bar.
senses.exampleCN: 河口处的沙子沉积，慢慢堆出一道新沙洲。
senses.why: deponere means 'to put down'. When a current loses energy it puts its load down, so deposition is literally the putting-down of particles.
senses.whyCN: deponere 意为“放下”。水流失去能量时就把负载放下，因此沉积字面上就是颗粒被放下。

senses.title: The material that has settled
senses.titleCN: 沉积物：落下来的那一层
senses.definition: the layer or body of material produced by deposition
senses.definitionCN: 由沉积作用产生的那一层或那一堆物质
senses.example: The cliff exposes a thick deposition of volcanic ash.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁露出厚厚一层火山灰沉积。
senses.why: The -ion noun can name either the act or its result. Once the particles are down, the same word points to the layer they form.
senses.whyCN: -ion 名词既可指动作，也可指结果。颗粒一旦落下，同一个词就指向它们形成的那一层。

senses.title: Sworn testimony taken out of court
senses.titleCN: 宣誓证词：法庭外的正式口供
senses.definition: a formal statement made under oath before a court officer, usually before trial
senses.definitionCN: 在法院官员面前宣誓作出的正式陈述，通常在开庭前进行
senses.example: The witness gave a deposition that contradicted her earlier statement.
senses.exampleCN: 证人作出的宣誓证词与她早先的说法相矛盾。
senses.why: Legal language borrowed deponere in the sense 'to set down in writing or on record'. A deposition is testimony put down so it cannot be changed later.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言借用了 deponere 的“记录下来”义。证词被“放下”固定住，日后就不能更改。

senses.title: Removal from office
senses.titleCN: 罢免：把掌权者从位子上拿下
senses.definition: the removal of a ruler, bishop or official from power
senses.definitionCN: 把统治者、主教或官员从权力位置上撤下
senses.example: The deposition of the king led to a decade of civil war.
senses.exampleCN: 国王被罢黜引发了一场十年内战。
senses.why: To depose is to put someone down from a seat. The noun keeps that physical picture: the person is lowered out of the position they occupied.
senses.whyCN: depose 就是把某人从位子上拿下。名词保留了这一物理画面：人被从所占据的位置上放下来。

senses.title: Thin films formed from vapour
senses.titleCN: 气相沉积：原子落到基片上
senses.definition: a manufacturing process in which a vapour condenses onto a surface to form a thin film
senses.definitionCN: 蒸气在表面凝结形成薄膜的制造工艺
senses.example: Chemical vapour deposition coats the tools with a hard layer.
senses.exampleCN: 化学气相沉积在刀具上覆上一层硬膜。
senses.why: The industrial sense is the geological sense at atomic scale: particles arrive and settle on a surface, building a layer.
senses.whyCN: 工业义就是地质义在原子尺度上的版本：粒子到达并落在表面，堆成一层。

senses.title: Metal laid down by current
senses.titleCN: 电沉积：金属离子在电极上落户
senses.definition: the electrochemical process in which dissolved metal ions form a solid coating on an electrode
senses.definitionCN: 溶解的金属离子在电极上形成固体镀层的电化学过程
senses.example: Electrodeposition of copper filled the narrow trenches on the chip.
senses.exampleCN: 铜的电沉积填满了芯片上的窄沟槽。
senses.why: Here the particles are ions driven to a surface by current. The word still means 'put down', only the force moving them has changed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的颗粒是被电流驱赶到表面的离子。词义仍是“放下”，只是推动它们的力变了。

senses.title: Pollutants settling on surfaces
senses.titleCN: 污染物沉降：脏东西从空中落下来
senses.definition: the transfer of airborne pollutants onto land, water or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 空气中的污染物转移到土地、水体或建筑物上的过程
senses.example: Nitrogen deposition from nearby farms changed the meadow's plant life.
senses.exampleCN: 附近农场带来的氮沉降改变了草甸的植物群落。
senses.why: Environmental science applies the old word to particles and gases leaving the air. What falls is no longer sand, but the motion is the same.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把这个旧词用于离开空气的颗粒和气体。落下之物不再是沙子，但运动方式相同。

senses.title: The act of placing something down
senses.titleCN: 安放：把物件郑重放下
senses.definition: the act of laying or placing an object somewhere, often in a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放置在某处的动作，常用于仪式场合
senses.example: The deposition of wreaths at the memorial takes place at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 纪念仪式上的花圈安放于黎明时进行。
senses.why: This sense stays closest to deponere: an object is put down at a chosen place. Ceremonial use preserves the literal gesture beneath all the technical senses.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项最贴近 deponere：物件被放到选定之处。仪式用法在所有技术义之下保留了字面动作。

intro.en: Deposition goes back to Latin depositio, from deponere 'to put down', itself de- 'down' plus ponere 'to place'. The geological, legal and political senses all preserve that basic downward placement.
intro.cn: deposition 可追到拉丁 depositio，来自 deponere“放下”，由 de-“向下”和 ponere“放置”构成。地质、法律与政治义都保留了“向下放置”这一基本动作。

items.en: ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. It is the source of position, positive, compose, expose and deposit, so the whole family is about placement.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放、安置、摆”。它是 position、positive、compose、expose、deposit 的来源，因此整个词族都围绕“放置”。

items.en: deponere adds de- 'down', giving 'to put down, lay aside, store'. Latin used it for laying down a burden as well as for depositing money or testimony.
items.cn: deponere 加 de-“向下”，意为“放下、搁置、存放”。拉丁语既用它表示放下重担，也表示存放钱款或证词。

items.en: The noun depositio names the act of putting down and, by extension, what has been put down. English takes the stem deposit- and adds -ion.
items.cn: 名词 depositio 命名“放下”的动作，并引申指被放下之物。英语取 deposit- 词干加 -ion。

items.en: From the idea of putting something on record comes the legal deposition: testimony set down under oath. The exact date of this extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 从“记录在案”的观念产生了法律上的 deposition：宣誓后记录下来的证词。这一引申的确切年代存疑。

items.en: Deposing a ruler is putting him down from a seat of power. The political noun appears in medieval and early modern English, again from deponere.
items.cn: 罢黜统治者就是把他从权力座位上拿下。这一政治名词出现于中世纪和近代早期英语，同样来自 deponere。

items.en: Geology adopted deposition for settling sediment in the 18th and 19th centuries; materials science later applied it to thin films. The physical image needed no change.
items.cn: 地质学在 18 至 19 世纪采用 deposition 表示沉积物沉降；材料科学后来把它用于薄膜。物理意象无需改变。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on deposit- with different endings; the near-meaning group separates the kinds of settling, recording and removal the word can name.
note.cn: 形近组由 deposit- 加不同词尾构成；近义组区分这个词所能命名的几种沉降、记录与撤职。

entries.definition: to put money or material somewhere; the material or money put down. It is the everyday member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 存放钱或物质；被放下的物质或钱款。它是这个词族的日常成员。

entries.definition: relating to deposition, especially in geology. The -al suffix turns the process noun into an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 与沉积有关的，尤用于地质学。-al 把过程名词变成形容词。

entries.definition: to remove from office, or to testify under oath. It is the verb behind the political and legal senses.
entries.definitionCN: 罢免；宣誓作证。它是政治义与法律义背后的动词。

entries.definition: the process by which sediment settles; it overlaps with geological deposition but focuses on the settling of solids in a fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 沉积物沉降的过程；它与地质沉积重叠，但聚焦于固体在流体中的沉降。

entries.definition: a formal statement of evidence, usually in court; a deposition is one specific kind taken before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的证据陈述，通常在法庭上；deposition 是开庭前取得的特定一种。

entries.definition: the removal of a monarch from the throne; narrower than deposition, which also covers bishops and officials.
entries.definitionCN: 把君主从王座上撤下；比 deposition 窄，后者也涵盖主教与官员。

entries.definition: the gradual gathering of material; it stresses the growing pile rather than the act of laying each particle down.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的逐渐堆积；它强调堆头越来越大，而不是每颗粒被放下的动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + ponere 'place': deposition is a placing down, whether sand, testimony or a crown.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ ponere“放置”：deposition 就是放下——无论放的是沙、证词还是王冠。

normal.en: deposit, position, compose and expose all share ponere, so the family is a set of placements.
normal.cn: deposit、position、compose、expose 都共享 ponere，整个词族就是一组“放置”。

normal.en: The legal phrase is 'give a deposition', not 'make': the witness hands the record over.
normal.cn: 法律搭配是 give a deposition，而不是 make：证人把记录交出去。

normal.en: In geology, look for the pair deposition and erosion: one builds layers, the other removes them.
normal.cn: 地质学里记住 deposition 与 erosion 这对词：一个铺层，一个剥层。

normal.en: Vapour deposition is the same word at atomic scale: atoms settle on a surface just as sand settles on a riverbed.
normal.cn: 气相沉积是同一个词在原子尺度上：原子落在表面，正如沙落在河床。

abstract.en: Think of a hand opening and letting a fistful of sand fall onto a table in slow motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手张开，让一把沙以慢镜头落到桌面上。

abstract.en: Think of dust forming a grey film on a windowsill over weeks of stillness.
abstract.cn: 想象几周无人打扰，灰尘在窗台上积成一层灰膜。

abstract.en: Think of a crown being lifted from a head and set down on a table: that downward move is the political sense.
abstract.cn: 想象王冠被从头上升起，再放到桌上：这个向下的动作就是政治义。

examples.en: Wind deposition created the long dunes along the coast.
examples.cn: 风的沉积作用在海岸边造出了长长的沙丘。

examples.en: The lawyer scheduled a deposition for the following Tuesday.
examples.cn: 律师把宣誓证词安排在下一个星期二。

examples.en: The deposition of the bishop was ordered by the council.
examples.cn: 主教被议会下令罢免。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地破zition”——地（de）上破（po）碎的沙一点点sit（沉积）下来 → deposition 沉积、证词

root: 拉丁 deponere“放下、存放”（de-“向下”+ ponere“放置”）；deposit- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one downward movement: something is taken from where it was and set down somewhere else, to stay.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个向下动作：某物从原处被取下，放到别处并留在那里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current slowing and letting its load fall to the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：水流放慢，让负载落到水底。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: laying particles down and the layer that results are the same event seen while happening and afterwards.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：把颗粒放下与由此形成的层，是同一事件在发生中与发生后的两种看法。

branches.en: REMOVAL: a ruler or bishop set down from a position of power.
branches.cn: 罢免：把统治者或主教从权力位置上撤下。

branches.en: INDUSTRIAL LAYERS: vapour and electrodeposition build films atom by atom, the geological gesture repeated in a factory.
branches.cn: 工业镀层：气相沉积与电沉积逐原子造膜，是地质动作在工厂里的重复。

branches.en: ENVIRONMENT AND CEREMONY: pollutants falling on land and wreaths laid at a memorial both end with something resting where it was placed.
branches.cn: 环境与仪式：污染物落到土地上、花圈安放在纪念碑前，最终都是某物停在它被放下之处。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CORE: the deposition under oath is the most institutionalised form of 'putting something down so it cannot move'.
branches.cn: 法律核心：宣誓证词是“把东西放下、使其不能移动”最制度化的形式。

intro.en: Deposition is deposit plus -ion. The Latin parts de- and ponere are fused inside the base; English freely adds -ion, -al, -or and -ory to build the family.
intro.cn: deposition 是 deposit 加 -ion。拉丁成分 de- 与 ponere 已融合在词基内；英语可自由加 -ion、-al、-or、-ory 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' yields deponere 'put down', depositio 'a laying down', and depositum 'something deposited'. English relatives include deposit, position, compose, expose and postpone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere“放置”派生 deponere“放下”、depositio“放下”、depositum“存放物”。英语同族词包括 deposit、position、compose、expose、postpone。

items.meaning: to put down; material or money put down
items.meaningCN: 存放；沉积；存款（de-“向下”+ ponere“放置”）
items.example: The river deposits silt along its lower course.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在下游沿线沉积淤泥。

items.meaning: the act of laying down, or what is laid down
items.meaningCN: 沉积；沉积物（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The deposition of ash buried the old road.
items.exampleCN: 火山灰的沉积掩埋了旧路。

items.meaning: relating to deposition
items.meaningCN: 沉积的；与沉积有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The rock shows clear depositional layers.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石显示出清晰的沉积层。

items.meaning: a person who deposits money or material
items.meaningCN: 存款人；沉积者（-or 构成施事者名词）
items.example: Each depositor received a receipt.
items.exampleCN: 每位存款人都拿到了一张收据。

items.meaning: a place where things are stored
items.meaningCN: 存放处；储藏所（-ory 构成处所名词）
items.example: The documents are kept in a secure depository.
items.exampleCN: 这些文件存放在一个安全的储藏所。

items.meaning: to remove from office; to testify
items.meaningCN: 罢免；宣誓作证（由“拿下”引申）
