items.example: The council moved to depose the mayor.
items.exampleCN: 议会着手罢免市长。

items.meaning: to deposit again; to lay down a second time
items.meaningCN: 再次沉积；重新存放（re-“再次”+ deposit）
items.example: The eroded sand was redeposited further downstream.
items.exampleCN: 被侵蚀的沙子在下游更远处再次沉积。

items.meaning: a second laying down of material
items.meaningCN: 再次沉积；再沉积作用（re- + deposition）
items.example: Redeposition thickened the layer near the bend.
items.exampleCN: 再沉积使弯道附近的层变厚。

latinEntries.meaning: to put down; to lay aside; to store

definition_zh: 派生的；缺乏原创的；衍生物；金融衍生品；（数学）导数
definition_en: derived from something else; lacking originality; or a thing produced from another source
core_image: 一条小溪从大河旁边分出去，水还是那批水，河道却是新的
scene: The new drug is a derivative of a compound found in willow bark.
sceneCN: 这里 derivative 是「衍生物」（第 4 个义项：由另一物质经改造而来）；句意：这种新药是柳树皮中一种化合物的衍生物。图中可辨识物件：柳树皮、实验烧瓶、分子结构图、药片。

pos.zh: 派生的；由……衍生的；缺乏原创的
衍生物；衍生品；派生词；导数

collocations.zh: 缺乏原创性的；高度模仿的

senses.title: Coming from another source
senses.titleCN: 派生的：源头在别处
senses.definition: formed or developed from something else rather than existing independently
senses.definitionCN: 由他物形成或发展而来，而非独立存在的
senses.example: The design is derivative of an earlier bridge in the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计是从同城一座更早的桥派生出来的。
senses.why: derivare means 'to lead water away from a stream'. A derivative thing is water led off from an existing channel: it flows, but the source is not its own.
senses.whyCN: derivare 意为“从溪流引走水”。derivative 的东西就是从既有水道引出的水：它流动，但源头不属于自己。

senses.title: Lacking originality
senses.titleCN: 缺乏原创的：只是别人的回声
senses.definition: imitative and unoriginal, repeating ideas already used by others
senses.definitionCN: 模仿他人、缺乏原创，重复已有观念
senses.example: Critics called the sequel derivative and predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称这部续集缺乏原创、一猜就中。
senses.why: The pejorative sense extends the same image: if everything is led off from another stream, nothing here has its own spring. The word judges the absence of an independent source.
senses.whyCN: 贬义义项是同一意象的延伸：如果一切都从别人的溪流引来，这里就没有自己的泉眼。这个词评判的正是独立源头的缺席。

senses.title: A financial instrument
senses.titleCN: 金融衍生品：价值挂在别的东西上
senses.definition: a financial contract whose value depends on an underlying asset, rate or index
senses.definitionCN: 价值取决于标的资产、利率或指数的金融合约
senses.example: The fund used interest-rate derivatives to hedge its loans.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金用利率衍生品为贷款做对冲。
senses.why: The contract has no independent value; it is led off from a bond, a rate or a price. Finance chose the word because the value literally flows from the underlying.
senses.whyCN: 这种合约没有独立价值，它的价值从债券、利率或价格引出。金融界用这个词，是因为价值确实来自标的。

senses.title: A chemical compound made from another
senses.titleCN: 化学衍生物：改一处就成了新物质
senses.definition: a substance obtained from another by a chemical change, often sharing its core structure
senses.definitionCN: 经化学变化从另一物质得到的物质，通常共享核心结构
senses.example: The derivative is more soluble than the original compound.
senses.exampleCN: 这种衍生物比原化合物更易溶解。
senses.why: Chemists modify one group and keep the skeleton, so the new molecule is a channel led off the old one. The stem is shared; only the branch differs.
senses.whyCN: 化学家改动一个基团、保留骨架，于是新分子就是从旧分子引出的水道。主干共享，只有分支不同。

senses.title: A word formed from another
senses.titleCN: 派生词：从词根长出来的新词
senses.definition: in linguistics, a word formed from an existing word or root by adding affixes or changing its form
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上由既有词或词根加词缀、改变形式而形成的新词
senses.example: The noun 'kindness' is a derivative of the adjective 'kind'.
senses.exampleCN: 名词 kindness 是形容词 kind 的派生词。
senses.why: Word formation is treated as water led from a source: the root supplies the meaning and the suffix opens a new channel, producing a new word.
senses.whyCN: 构词被看成从源头引水：词根提供意义，后缀开出新水道，产生新词。

senses.title: The rate of change in calculus
senses.titleCN: 导数：变化率本身
senses.definition: in mathematics, the rate at which a function changes with respect to one of its variables
senses.definitionCN: 数学中函数相对于某个变量的变化率
senses.example: The derivative of a straight line's position is its constant speed.
senses.exampleCN: 直线运动的位移导数是其恒定速度。
senses.why: A derivative is a value drawn out of a function by a limiting process. The word keeps the sense of something obtained from a larger source, not invented independently.
senses.whyCN: 导数是经极限过程从函数中引出的值。这个词保留了“从更大源头取得而非独立发明”的含义。

senses.title: A work adapted from another
senses.titleCN: 演绎作品：在原作上再创作
senses.definition: in copyright law, a work that adapts or transforms an existing protected work
senses.definitionCN: 版权法中改编或转化既有受保护作品的新作品
senses.example: The film is a derivative work based on a 19th-century novel.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是改编自一部 19 世纪小说的演绎作品。
senses.why: Copyright uses the image precisely: the new work draws its substance from the old one, so permission flows with the water.
senses.whyCN: 版权法精确使用了这个意象：新作品从旧作品取得实质内容，因此许可随水一起流动。

senses.title: A secondary product of research
senses.titleCN: 副产品：主流程之外长出来的结果
senses.definition: something produced as a secondary result of a process, project or discovery
senses.definitionCN: 作为某过程、项目或发现的次要结果而产生的东西
senses.example: A useful battery material emerged as a derivative of the space programme.
senses.exampleCN: 一种有用的电池材料作为航天计划的衍生成果出现。
senses.why: Here the source is a process rather than a substance. The result is still led off the main channel, which is why it counts as a derivative rather than a primary product.
senses.whyCN: 这里的源头是过程而不是物质。结果仍从主水道引出，因此算衍生物而不是主产品。

intro.en: Derivative comes from Latin derivare 'to lead water away from a stream', de- 'from' plus rivus 'stream'. English first used it for 'derived things', then for chemistry, linguistics and mathematics; the financial sense is 20th-century.
intro.cn: derivative 来自拉丁 derivare“从溪流引走水”，由 de-“从”和 rivus“溪流”构成。英语最初用它表示“派生之物”，后来用于化学、语言学和数学；金融义是 20 世纪的产物。

items.en: rivus meant 'a small stream or channel'. It also gave English river and rival, the latter from rivalis 'one who uses the same stream'.
items.cn: rivus 意为“小溪、水道”。它也派生了英语 river 和 rival，后者来自 rivalis“共用同一条溪流的人”。

items.en: derivare 'to lead off water' is de- 'from' plus rivare 'to channel'. The literal operation is engineering: a branch canal takes water from a main stream.
items.cn: derivare“引走水”是 de-“从”加 rivare“开渠”。字面操作是工程性的：支渠从主溪流取水。

items.en: Old French deriver passed the verb into English as derive. The adjective and noun derivative followed in the 16th century; the exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 deriver 把动词以 derive 形式传给英语。形容词与名词 derivative 在 16 世纪跟进，确切最早年代存疑。

items.en: In the 19th century chemistry named a compound made by modifying another as a derivative. The shared skeleton is the main stream, and the change is the branch.
items.cn: 19 世纪化学把经改造另一化合物而得到的物质称为 derivative。共享的骨架是主溪流，改动则是支渠。

items.en: Linguistics applies the term to words formed from roots or other words. A root supplies meaning, and affixes open a new channel.
items.cn: 语言学用该词指由词根或其他词形成的词。词根提供意义，词缀开出新水道。

items.en: Financial derivatives appear in the 20th century. Their value is explicitly derived from an underlying asset, so the metaphor became a definition.
items.cn: 金融衍生品出现于 20 世纪。其价值明确来自标的资产，于是隐喻变成了定义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the derive family and different endings; the near-meaning group separates copied, secondary and mathematically derived things.
note.cn: 形近组共享 derive 词族、词尾不同；近义组区分模仿的、次要的和数学上派生的事物。

entries.definition: to obtain from a source; to originate. It names the act of leading something off, while derivative names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 从某来源获得；起源于。它命名引出动作，而 derivative 命名结果。

entries.definition: the process of deriving, or the origin of a word; the -ation suffix focuses on the process rather than the product.
entries.definitionCN: 推导过程；词源。-ation 后缀聚焦过程而不是产物。

entries.definition: relating to word formation; a derivational affix creates a new word rather than a new grammatical form.
entries.definitionCN: 构词方面的；派生词缀创造新词，而不是新的语法形式。

entries.definition: copying the style or behaviour of others; close to the pejorative sense of derivative, but stresses copying as an act.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿他人风格或行为的；接近 derivative 的贬义，但强调“模仿”这一动作。

entries.definition: coming after or depending on something primary; derivative stresses the source, secondary stresses the rank.
entries.definitionCN: 次要的；在首要事物之后或依赖其存在；derivative 强调来源，secondary 强调等级。

entries.definition: a secondary result of a process; closest to sense 8, but it does not imply that the substance was deliberately derived.
entries.definitionCN: 过程的次要结果；最接近第 8 义，但不暗示该物质是被有意衍生出来的。

entries.definition: a thing that develops from a larger one, like a branch from a stem; it is figurative and less technical than derivative.
entries.definitionCN: 从较大事物发展出来的分支，如同主干上的枝条；它更形象，技术性不如 derivative。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'from' + rivus 'stream': a derivative is water led off from another stream.
normal.cn: de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”：derivative 就是从另一条溪流引出的水。

normal.en: river and rival are cousins from rivus: the rival is the person who shares your stream.
normal.cn: river 和 rival 都是 rivus 的表亲：rival 就是与你共用一条溪流的人。

normal.en: In mathematics, look for the pattern f'(x): the prime mark is the sign that a value has been drawn from the function.
normal.cn: 数学里找 f'(x) 这个写法：撇号就是“从函数中引出值”的标志。

normal.en: The financial phrase is derivative contract; if the value depends on something else, it is a derivative.
normal.cn: 金融搭配是 derivative contract；如果价值取决于别的东西，它就是衍生品。

normal.en: A derivative work in copyright is an adaptation, which is why the same word appears in film and software licences.
normal.cn: 版权中的 derivative work 是改编作品，所以同一个词会出现在电影和软件许可里。

abstract.en: Think of a garden hose split by a Y-connector: the second line carries the same water.
abstract.cn: 想象一根花园水管被 Y 形接头分开：第二条管里流的是同一批水。

abstract.en: Think of a river delta: every channel is the main river redistributed, not a new river.
abstract.cn: 想象一片河口三角洲：每条水道都是主河的重分，而不是一条新河。

abstract.en: Think of a cover song: the melody is borrowed, the performance is new, and both facts matter.
abstract.cn: 想象一首翻唱歌曲：旋律是借来的，演绎是新的，两个事实都重要。

examples.en: Many modern drugs are derivatives of plants used in traditional medicine.
examples.cn: 许多现代药物是传统医学中所用植物的衍生物。

examples.en: The bank lost heavily on derivatives tied to mortgage debt.
examples.cn: 这家银行在与房贷债务挂钩的衍生品上损失惨重。

examples.en: His early paintings are derivative, but the later work has its own voice.
examples.cn: 他早期的画缺乏原创，但后期作品有了自己的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地river体”——地（de）上的 river（河流）分出一条小水道，就是它的衍生 → derivative 派生的、衍生物

root: 拉丁 derivare“从溪流引水”（de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”）；derivat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one flow: something is led out of an existing channel, so its existence depends on a source it did not create.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一股水流：某物从既有水道被引出，因此它的存在依赖一个并非自己创造的源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small channel led off from a larger stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：从大河旁引出一条小水道。

branches.en: ORIGINALITY: being led off a stream becomes a judgement when the new channel has no spring of its own.
branches.cn: 原创性：当新水道没有自己的泉眼时，“从别处引水”就变成一种评判。

branches.en: VALUE AND COPYRIGHT: a derivative contract and a derivative work both draw their worth or substance from an underlying original.
branches.cn: 价值与版权：衍生合约与演绎作品都从标的原作取得价值或实质内容。

branches.en: SUBSTANCE AND PROCESS: chemical derivatives and research spin-offs are branches grown from a parent material or project.
branches.cn: 物质与过程：化学衍生物与研究副产品，都是从母体材料或项目长出的分支。

branches.en: WORDS AND NUMBERS: a derived word and a mathematical derivative are both values obtained by a defined operation on a base.
branches.cn: 词与数：派生词与数学导数，都是对基体施加既定运算后得到的值。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: every other sense specifies the kind of source and the kind of channel involved.
branches.cn: 基础义：其余义项都只是说明源头与分支的类型。

intro.en: Derivative is derivat- plus -ive. Latin de- and rivus are fused inside the stem; English productively adds -ive, -ation, -ational and -able to build the family.
intro.cn: derivative 是 derivat- 加 -ive。拉丁 de- 与 rivus 已融合在词干内；英语能产地加 -ive、-ation、-ational、-able 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' yields rivulus 'little stream', derivare 'lead off water', and rivalis 'sharing a stream'. English relatives include river, rival, derive and derivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus“溪流”派生 rivulus“小溪”、derivare“引水”、rivalis“共用溪流者”。英语同族词包括 river、rival、derive、derivation。

items.meaning: to obtain from a source; to originate
items.meaningCN: 获得；源自；推导（de-“从”+ rivare“引水”）
items.example: The word derives from an old French term for a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个词源自一个表示边界的古法语词。

items.meaning: the process of deriving; word origin
items.meaningCN: 推导；派生；词源（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The dictionary gives the derivation of the name.
items.exampleCN: 词典给出了这个名字的词源。

items.meaning: derived; a derived thing
items.meaningCN: 派生的；衍生物（-ive 构成形容词与名词）
items.example: The derivative product sold better than the original.
items.exampleCN: 衍生产品比原产品卖得更好。

items.meaning: relating to derivation or word formation
items.meaningCN: 派生的；构词的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The suffix is derivational, not inflectional.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀是派生性的，不是屈折性的。

items.meaning: in a derived or secondary way
items.meaningCN: 派生地；间接地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The right is held derivatively, through the parent company.
items.exampleCN: 这项权利是通过母公司间接持有的。

items.meaning: able to be derived
items.meaningCN: 可推导的；可获得的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The result is derivable from two simple assumptions.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果可以从两个简单假设推导出来。

items.meaning: a large natural stream of water
items.meaningCN: 河流（同源词，rivus 的英语形态）
items.example: The river carries sediment to the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这条河把泥沙带向大海。

items.meaning: a competitor
items.meaningCN: 竞争对手（同源词，原指共用一条溪流的人）
items.example: The two firms became rivals for the same contract.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司成了同一合同的竞争对手。

definition_en: the process or fact of coming from a source, or the act of obtaining one thing from another
core_image: 一条支渠从主河分出，渠口清楚标着它从哪里来
scene: The derivation of the formula from two simple laws impressed the class.
sceneCN: 这里 derivation 是「推导」（第 3 个义项：由前提一步步得出结果）；句意：这个公式由两条简单定律推导出来，让全班印象深刻。图中可辨识物件：黑板上的公式、两条起始定律、箭头、学生笔记。

senses.title: The fact of coming from a source
senses.titleCN: 来源：这东西是从哪儿来的
senses.definition: the origin or source from which something comes
senses.definitionCN: 某物所来自的起源或源头
senses.example: The derivation of the family name is still disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个姓氏的来源仍有争议。
senses.why: derivare means 'to lead water off a stream'. Derivation names the traceable route from a source to the thing that now exists.
senses.whyCN: derivare 意为“从溪流引水”。derivation 命名的是从源头到现存事物之间可追踪的路径。

senses.title: Word formation by affixes
senses.titleCN: 构词派生：给词根加零件
senses.definition: in linguistics, the formation of a new word from an existing word or root by adding affixes
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上通过加词缀从既有词或词根形成新词
senses.example: The derivation of 'unhelpful' uses the prefix un- and the suffix -ful.
senses.exampleCN: unhelpful 的派生用了前缀 un- 和后缀 -ful。
senses.why: A root is the main stream; a prefix or suffix is the branch canal. Derivation is the operation that opens the new channel and changes the word's meaning or class.
senses.whyCN: 词根是主溪流；前缀或后缀是支渠。derivation 就是开出新水道、并改变词义或词性的操作。

senses.title: Step-by-step mathematical proof
senses.titleCN: 推导：从前提走到结论
senses.definition: the process of reaching a result by a series of logical or mathematical steps
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列逻辑或数学步骤得出结果的过程
senses.example: The derivation takes only three lines but requires a careful assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 这个推导只有三行，但需要一个谨慎的假设。
senses.why: Each step follows from the one before, like water running down a channel. The result is not invented; it is led out from the starting premises.
senses.whyCN: 每一步都从前一步流出，像水沿水道下行。结果不是凭空发明，而是从起始前提引出。

senses.title: Making one compound from another
senses.titleCN: 化学衍生：从旧物质造新物质
senses.definition: the chemical process or relationship by which one substance is obtained from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种物质得到另一种物质的化学过程或关系
senses.example: The derivation of the dye from coal tar was a 19th-century advance.
senses.exampleCN: 从煤焦油制取这种染料是 19 世纪的进步。
senses.why: The original compound keeps its skeleton while a group is changed, so the new substance is a channel led off the old material.
senses.whyCN: 原化合物保留骨架、只改一个基团，因此新物质是从旧材料引出的水道。

senses.title: The study of where a word came from
senses.titleCN: 词源：这个词的来路
senses.definition: the etymological history of a particular word, including the forms it passed through
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定词的历史来源，包括它经历的各个形式
senses.example: The dictionary entry gives the derivation of 'salary' from Latin sal.
senses.exampleCN: 词典条目给出了 salary 源自拉丁语 sal 的词源。
senses.why: Etymological derivation is sense 1 applied to words: the modern form is water led from an older stream, and the dictionary maps the route.
senses.whyCN: 词源是第 1 义用在词上：现代形式是从更古老溪流引出的水，词典画出这条路线。

senses.title: Logical inference
senses.titleCN: 推论：由已知推出未知
senses.definition: the drawing of a conclusion from premises by reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 通过推理从前提得出结论
senses.example: The derivation of her guilt from those facts is not convincing.
senses.exampleCN: 从那些事实推出她有罪的推论并不令人信服。
senses.why: Logic treats a conclusion as something obtained from premises rather than asserted on its own, so the water metaphor extends to reasoning.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把结论看成从前提获得的东西，而不是自行断言，于是引水隐喻扩展到推理。

senses.title: Diverting a watercourse
senses.titleCN: 引水：把河水改道
senses.definition: the physical act of leading water from its natural course to another channel
senses.definitionCN: 把水从其自然水道引到另一条水道的实际动作
senses.example: The derivation of the stream for irrigation began in the 18th century.
senses.exampleCN: 为灌溉引走这条溪水始于 18 世纪。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of derivare and the source of all the others. Engineering makes the metaphor visible: the new channel is cut and the water follows.
senses.whyCN: 这是 derivare 的字面义，也是其他义项的源头。工程让隐喻变得可见：新渠一开，水就跟着走。

senses.title: Origin of authority or meaning
senses.titleCN: 来源：权力或意义从何处取得
senses.definition: the source from which a right, power or meaning is understood to come
senses.definitionCN: 某项权利、权力或意义被认为所来自的源头
senses.example: The court examined the derivation of the agency's authority.
senses.exampleCN: 法院审查了该机构权力的来源。
senses.why: Rights and meanings are also treated as flowing from a source. The noun asks where the water comes from, not whether it is wet.
senses.whyCN: 权利和意义也被当成从某源头流出。这个名词问的是水从哪里来，而不是水是否湿。

intro.en: Derivation goes back to Latin derivatio, from derivare 'to lead water off', de- 'from' plus rivus 'stream'. The word moved from irrigation to language, logic and chemistry without changing its shape.
intro.cn: derivation 可追到拉丁 derivatio，来自 derivare“引走水”，由 de-“从”和 rivus“溪流”构成。这个词从灌溉转到语言、逻辑和化学，形态始终未变。

items.en: rivus 'stream' gives the image of a channel with a direction. The same root produces rivalis 'one who shares a stream', hence English rival.
items.cn: rivus“溪流”提供了有方向的水道意象。同一词根产生 rivalis“共用溪流者”，即英语 rival。

items.en: derivare 'to lead off water' describes an engineering act: cutting a branch canal so that part of the flow takes a new route.
items.cn: derivare“引走水”描述一个工程动作：开一条支渠，让部分水流改走新路线。

items.en: derivatio named the act of diverting water and, figuratively, the tracing of something to its source. The figurative use is already present in Latin.
items.cn: derivatio 命名引水动作，并比喻指把某物追溯到其源头。比喻用法在拉丁语中已经存在。

items.en: English adopts derivation in the 15th century for origin and descent. The exact earliest record is uncertain because derive and derivation entered through French forms.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪采用 derivation 表示起源与传承。由于 derive 与 derivation 是经法语形式进入的，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: In the 19th century, linguistics fixed derivation as the formation of words by affixation, separating it from inflection, which only changes grammatical form.
items.cn: 19 世纪，语言学把 derivation 固定为通过加词缀构词的过程，并与只改变语法形式的屈折区分开。

items.en: Mathematics and chemistry adopted the noun for stepwise proofs and for making one compound from another. Both keep the idea of a traceable route from a source.
items.cn: 数学与化学采用这个名词表示逐步证明和从一种化合物制取另一种。两者都保留了“从源头可追踪的路径”这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deriv- stem with different suffixes; the near-meaning group separates origin, formation, proof and etymology.
note.cn: 形近组共享 deriv- 词干、后缀不同；近义组区分起源、构词、证明与词源。

entries.definition: a thing produced from another source. Derivation is the process; derivative is the product.
entries.definitionCN: 从另一来源产生的事物。derivation 是过程，derivative 是产物。

entries.definition: to obtain or originate from a source; the verb names the action behind the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从某来源获得或起源；这个动词命名过程名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: relating to derivation, especially in word formation; it describes the mechanism, not the history.
entries.definitionCN: 与派生有关的，尤指构词；它描述机制，而不是历史。

entries.definition: the point where something begins; derivation adds the sense of a trackable route from that point.
entries.definitionCN: 某物开始的点；derivation 另含“从该点可追踪的路径”之意。

entries.definition: the study of word origins; a derivation is the specific history of one word, while etymology is the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 词源学；derivation 是一个词的具体来源史，而 etymology 是学科。

entries.definition: a complete argument showing a result follows from premises; a derivation is the step sequence itself.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某结果由前提推出的完整论证；derivation 是那串步骤本身。

entries.definition: the process of being formed; it is broader than derivation and does not require an identifiable source.
entries.definitionCN: 形成的过程；比 derivation 更宽，不要求可识别的源头。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'from' + rivus 'stream': derivation traces the branch back to the stream.
normal.cn: de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”：derivation 把支渠一路追溯回溪流。

normal.en: In linguistics, remember the pair derivation and inflection: one makes a new word, the other changes a form.
normal.cn: 语言学里记住 derivation 与 inflection 这对词：一个造新词，一个改形式。

normal.en: A mathematical derivation is written step by step, so each line is a drop of water moving down the channel.
normal.cn: 数学推导是一行一行写的，每一行都是水道里向下流动的一滴水。

normal.en: The phrase word derivation points straight at etymology, the history of a form.
normal.cn: 短语 word derivation 直接指向词源，也就是一个形式的来路。

normal.en: derive, derivation, derivative and derivational share rivus, so the family can be learned as one water system.
normal.cn: derive、derivation、derivative、derivational 共享 rivus，可以把这个词族当成一套水系来学。

abstract.en: Think of a hand-drawn map where a dotted trail leads from a source to a village.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手绘地图，一条虚线从源头一路引到村庄。

abstract.en: Think of a genealogy chart: each name is connected by a line to the ancestor it came from.
abstract.cn: 想象一张族谱：每个名字都用一条线连到它的祖先。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe that starts with one dough and produces three different breads.
abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱：同一团面做出三种不同的面包。

examples.en: The derivation of the word 'money' goes back to a temple of Juno.
examples.cn: money 这个词的词源可追到一座朱诺神庙。

examples.en: She published a full derivation of the equation in the appendix.
examples.cn: 她在附录中发表了该方程的完整推导。

examples.en: The derivation of the new plastic from plant oil reduced costs.
examples.cn: 从植物油制取这种新塑料降低了成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地riveration”——地（de）上的 river（河）引出一条支流，一路追溯到源头 → derivation 起源、推导、词源

root: 拉丁 derivare“从溪流引水”（de-“从”+ rivus“溪流”）；derivat- 词干 + -ion 过程名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one path: a traceable route from a source to a result, whether the source is a stream, a root, a premise or a parent compound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一条路径：从源头到结果的可追踪路线——源头可以是溪流、词根、前提或母体化合物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch canal cut from a main river, with its intake clearly marked.
core.cn: 核心意象：从主河开出的支渠，取水口标得清清楚楚。

branches.en: WORD ORIGIN: the history of a particular word, through the forms it has taken.
branches.cn: 词源：一个特定词的历史来源，包括它经历的各个形式。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AND CHEMISTRY: affixation opens a new word channel, and chemical change opens a new compound channel.
branches.cn: 语言与化学：加词缀开出新词水道，化学变化开出新化合物水道。

branches.en: PROOF AND INFERENCE: a mathematical derivation and a logical inference both move step by step from premises to a result.
branches.cn: 证明与推论：数学推导与逻辑推论都从前提一步步走向结果。

branches.en: WATER AND AUTHORITY: diverting a stream and deriving a right from a source are literal and institutional versions of the same intake.
branches.cn: 水与权力：引溪水与从源头取得权利，是同一取水口的字面版与制度版。

branches.en: THE BASE SENSE: all extensions ask the same question, 'where did this come from and by what route?'.
branches.cn: 基础义：所有引申都在问同一个问题——“它从哪里来，沿哪条路线来？”

intro.en: Derivation is derivat- plus -ion. Latin de- and rivus are fused; English uses -ion, -ive, -ational and -able as the productive endings of this family.
intro.cn: derivation 是 derivat- 加 -ion。拉丁 de- 与 rivus 已融合；英语用 -ion、-ive、-ational、-able 作为这个词族的能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' gives rivulus, derivare and derivatio. English relatives include river, rival, derive, derivative and derivation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus“溪流”派生 rivulus、derivare、derivatio。英语同族词包括 river、rival、derive、derivative、derivation。

items.meaning: to obtain from a source
items.meaningCN: 从某来源获得；派生（de-“从”+ rivare“开渠引水”）
items.example: The formula derives from a simple observation.
items.exampleCN: 这个公式来自一个简单观察。

items.meaning: the process of deriving; origin
items.meaningCN: 推导；派生；来源（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The derivation of the name took two pages.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字的来源考据写了两页。

items.meaning: derived; a derived product
items.meaningCN: 派生的；衍生物（-ive 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: The derivative compound is easier to store.
items.exampleCN: 这种衍生物更容易储存。

items.meaning: relating to derivation
items.meaningCN: 与派生有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: Derivational morphology studies how new words are built.
items.exampleCN: 派生形态学研究新词如何构成。

items.meaning: able to be derived
items.meaningCN: 可推导的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The conclusion is derivable from the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个结论可以从数据推导出来。

items.meaning: a large natural stream
items.meaningCN: 河流（同源词）
items.example: The river bends west before reaching the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在入海前向西转弯。

items.meaning: a competitor
items.meaningCN: 竞争对手（同源词，原指共用溪流者）
items.example: The two ports are rivals for the same trade.
items.exampleCN: 这两个港口是同一贸易的竞争对手。

items.meaning: to have as an origin
items.meaningCN: 源自（固定搭配，介词 from 标记源头）
items.example: The custom derives from an old harvest festival.
items.exampleCN: 这一习俗源自一个古老的丰收节。

latinEntries.meaning: a diverting; a tracing to a source

definition_zh: 描写的；描述性的；说明性的
definition_en: giving an account of what something is like rather than judging or changing it
core_image: 一支笔沿着物体的轮廓慢慢走，把看到的形状写下来
scene: The report gives a descriptive account of the village rather than a plan for improving it.
sceneCN: 这里 descriptive 是「描述性的」（第 1 个义项：说明是什么样，而不作评判或规划）；句意：这份报告对村庄作了描述性说明，而不是提出改善计划。图中可辨识物件：村庄全景、记录板、笔、未标注改造方案的空白页。

pos.zh: 描写的；描述性的；说明性的

senses.title: Saying what something is like
senses.titleCN: 描写的：说清它是什么样
senses.definition: giving an account of the features of something rather than evaluating it
senses.definitionCN: 说明某物的特征，而不是对它作出评价
senses.example: The guide is descriptive rather than judgemental about the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南对这座小镇是描述性的，而不是评判性的。
senses.why: describere means 'to write down'. The -ive suffix marks the quality of writing something down as it is, without adding a verdict.
senses.whyCN: describere 意为“写下”。-ive 标记“照原样写下来”的性质，不额外加判断。

senses.title: Detailed and vivid
senses.titleCN: 描写生动的：细节多到能看见
senses.definition: giving a full and vivid picture through concrete details
senses.definitionCN: 通过具体细节给出完整而生动的画面
senses.example: Her descriptive paragraph made the market smell and sound real.
senses.exampleCN: 她那段描写让集市的气味和声音都变得真实。
senses.why: A good description writes down enough detail that the reader can reconstruct the scene. The suffix -ive turns that act into a quality of the text.
senses.whyCN: 好的描写写下的细节足够读者重建场景。-ive 把这一动作变成文本的性质。

senses.title: Linguistics: observing, not prescribing
senses.titleCN: 描写语言学的：只记录怎么说
senses.definition: in linguistics, based on how language is actually used rather than on rules about how it should be used
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上基于语言的实际使用，而不是规定应当如何使用
senses.example: Descriptive grammar records the forms speakers actually use.
senses.exampleCN: 描写语法记录说话者实际使用的形式。
senses.why: The contrast with prescriptive is exact: one writes language down as observed, the other writes rules in advance. The root scribere holds both.
senses.whyCN: 它与 prescriptive 的对比非常精确：一个照观察写下语言，一个预先立规。词根 scribere 同时支撑两者。

senses.title: Statistics that summarise data
senses.titleCN: 描述统计：只把数据的样子说出来
senses.definition: in statistics, summarising the main features of a data set without drawing conclusions beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上概括数据的主要特征，而不超出数据作结论
senses.example: Descriptive statistics showed a mean age of thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 描述统计显示平均年龄为三十二岁。
senses.why: The numbers describe the sample instead of testing a hypothesis about the population. The adjective keeps the 'write down what is there' stance.
senses.whyCN: 这些数字描述样本，而不是检验关于总体的假设。这个形容词保持了“把存在的写下来”的立场。

senses.title: Characteristic of something
senses.titleCN: 体现……特征的：这个词就说明它
senses.definition: used with 'of' to say that a word or feature characterises something
senses.definitionCN: 与 of 连用，表示某个词或特征体现了某事物的特点
senses.example: The term 'coastal' is descriptive of the region's economy.
senses.exampleCN: coastal 这个词体现了该地区经济的特点。
senses.why: Here the showing turns into representing: the label describes the thing so well that it becomes a characteristic rather than a comment.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“显示”转为“代表”：标签把事物描述得如此贴切，以致成为特征而不是评论。

senses.title: Merely labelling
senses.titleCN: 仅作标识的：名字只告诉你它是什么
senses.definition: naming or classifying something without explaining or justifying it
senses.definitionCN: 只给某物命名或分类，而不解释或论证
senses.example: The title is descriptive only; it makes no claim about quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标题只是标识性的，并不对质量作任何主张。
senses.why: A descriptive name writes down what is visible and stops there. The word marks the boundary between naming and evaluating.
senses.whyCN: 描述性名称只写下看得见的东西，到此为止。这个词标记了命名与评价之间的界线。

senses.title: Technical drawing
senses.titleCN: 画法几何的：用图把形状说清
senses.definition: in descriptive geometry, relating to the accurate two-dimensional representation of three-dimensional objects
senses.definitionCN: 画法几何中，用二维图形准确表示三维物体的
senses.example: Descriptive geometry is still taught to engineering students.
senses.exampleCN: 工程专业学生仍要学画法几何。
senses.why: Drawing an object's edges on paper is literally writing it down in lines. The technical sense is the oldest physical meaning of describere.
senses.whyCN: 把物体轮廓画在纸上，字面上就是用线条写下来。这个技术义是 describere 最古老的物理含义。

senses.title: Observational research
senses.titleCN: 描述性研究：先看清，再解释
senses.definition: in research, describing a situation or population without testing causal claims
senses.definitionCN: 研究中描述某种状况或人群，而不检验因果主张
senses.example: The study is descriptive and does not prove that the two events are linked.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究是描述性的，并不能证明两个事件有关联。
senses.why: A descriptive study records what is observed before asking why. The adjective signals that no causal claim has been written into the record.
senses.whyCN: 描述性研究在追问原因之前先记录观察到的内容。这个形容词表明记录里没有写进因果主张。

intro.en: Descriptive comes from Latin describere 'to write down, copy off', de- 'down' plus scribere 'write'. English formed the adjective with -ive; the contrast with prescriptive became central in linguistics.
intro.cn: descriptive 来自拉丁 describere“写下、描摹”，由 de-“向下”和 scribere“写”构成。英语用 -ive 构成形容词；与 prescriptive 的对立在语言学中变得关键。

items.en: scribere meant 'to write, mark, draw'. It is the source of script, scribe, prescribe, subscribe and manuscript, so the whole family concerns writing.
items.cn: scribere 意为“写、标记、画”。它是 script、scribe、prescribe、subscribe、manuscript 的来源，整个词族都与书写有关。

items.en: describere adds de- 'down', giving 'to write down, copy off, delineate'. Latin used it for drawing a boundary as well as for describing in words.
items.cn: describere 加 de-“向下”，意为“写下、描摹、画出轮廓”。拉丁语既用它表示划界，也表示用文字描述。

items.en: English forms descriptive on the stem descript- plus -ive in the 16th century. The exact first record is uncertain because description and descriptive entered close together.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪以 descript- 词干加 -ive 构成 descriptive。由于 description 与 descriptive 进入时间相近，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: Descriptive geometry was named in the 18th century for the drawing of solid forms on flat paper, reviving the literal 'draw a boundary' sense.
items.cn: 画法几何在 18 世纪得名，指在平面上绘制立体形状，复活了字面的“画出轮廓”义。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries, descriptive became the opposite of prescriptive: record usage versus lay down rules. The pair is now standard in language teaching.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，descriptive 成为 prescriptive 的对立面：记录用法对立法定规则。这一对词如今是语言教学的标准术语。

items.en: Descriptive statistics was fixed in the 20th century for summaries of a sample. The word marks what the numbers do: they describe, they do not test.
items.cn: 描述统计在 20 世纪固定下来，指对样本的概括。这个词标记数字的功能：它们描述，而不检验。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the scrib- stem; the near-meaning group distinguishes describing, illustrating, observing and prescribing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 scrib- 词干；近义组区分描述、说明、观察与规定。

entries.definition: to say what something is like; the verb names the act of writing down.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物是什么样；这个动词命名“写下”的动作。

entries.definition: a spoken or written account; it is the thing produced by describing.
entries.definitionCN: 口头或书面的描述；它是描述动作产生的成品。

entries.definition: laying down rules about what should be done or used; the direct opposite of descriptive in linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 规定应当如何做或如何使用；在语言学中是 descriptive 的直接对立面。

entries.definition: containing many specific facts; it stresses quantity of detail, while descriptive stresses the act of depicting.
entries.definitionCN: 包含许多具体事实；它强调细节数量，而 descriptive 强调描绘动作。

entries.definition: serving to explain by example or picture; it aims at understanding, while descriptive aims at an accurate account.
entries.definitionCN: 通过例子或图片说明；它追求理解，而 descriptive 追求准确叙述。

entries.definition: based on watching without intervention; it is the methodological cousin of descriptive research.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观察而不干预；它是描述性研究在方法上的表亲。

entries.definition: conveying feeling or personal style; descriptive conveys facts, expressive conveys the writer's response.
entries.definitionCN: 传达感情或个人风格；descriptive 传达事实，expressive 传达作者的反应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + scribere 'write': descriptive text is written down from observation.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ scribere“写”：描述性文本是从观察中写下来的。

normal.en: Remember descriptive versus prescriptive as a pair: observe and record, or command and correct.
normal.cn: 把 descriptive 与 prescriptive 成对记：观察记录，或命令纠正。

normal.en: In statistics, descriptive numbers summarise; inferential numbers test. The adjective tells you which job is being done.
normal.cn: 统计中，描述性数字做概括；推断性数字做检验。这个形容词告诉你正在做哪件事。

normal.en: A descriptive title tells you what the thing is, not whether it is good.
normal.cn: 描述性标题告诉你它是什么，而不是它好不好。

normal.en: descriptive geometry is literally drawing an object on paper, the oldest sense of the root.
normal.cn: 画法几何字面上就是把物体画在纸上，是词根最古老的义项。

abstract.en: Think of a pencil tracing the outline of a cup without shading it or grading its design.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔只沿着杯子轮廓走，不上阴影，也不评价设计。

abstract.en: Think of a nature documentary that names and shows the animal without telling you what to think.
abstract.cn: 想象一部自然纪录片，只命名并展示动物，不告诉你怎么想。

abstract.en: Think of a map that draws the coastline exactly as it is, leaving the traveller to choose the route.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图如实画出海岸线，把选路的自由留给旅人。

examples.en: The manual is descriptive, so it tells you how the machine behaves rather than how to fix it.
examples.cn: 这本手册是描述性的，讲的是机器如何运作，而不是如何修理。

examples.en: Her descriptive writing brings the old harbour back to life.
examples.cn: 她的描写性写作让旧港重现生机。

examples.en: The chart provides descriptive statistics for each age group.
examples.cn: 这张图表提供了各年龄组的描述统计。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地scribe体”——地（de）上拿笔（scribe）照着东西写，只写看到的不加评价 → descriptive 描述性的

root: 拉丁 describere“写下、描摹”（de-“向下”+ scribere“写”）；descript- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one stance: the writer records what is there, and stops before judging or commanding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个立场：写作者记录存在之物，在评判或命令之前停手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil tracing the outline of an object exactly as it stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅笔沿着物体原样描出轮廓。

branches.en: VIVIDNESS: a detailed scene is the same writing-down at a higher level of resolution.
branches.cn: 生动：细节场景是同一种“写下”在高分辨率层级上。

branches.en: OBSERVATION AS METHOD: descriptive linguistics and descriptive research both record usage or behaviour without imposing a rule.
branches.cn: 观察作为方法：描写语言学与描述性研究都记录用法或行为，不强加规则。

branches.en: SUMMARISING AND DRAWING: statistical summaries and technical drawings both reduce a complex object to a faithful outline.
branches.cn: 概括与绘图：统计概括与技术制图都把复杂对象缩减为忠实的轮廓。

branches.en: CHARACTERISING AND LABELLING: a word descriptive of a region and a merely descriptive title both stop at identification.
branches.cn: 特征与标识：描述地区特征的词与仅作标识的标题，都停在识别层面。

branches.en: THE BASE STANCE: all extensions keep the refusal to prescribe, even when the description is reduced to a single number or line.
branches.cn: 基础立场：所有引申都保留“不作规定”的态度，即使描述被缩减为一个数字或一条线。

intro.en: Descriptive is descript- plus -ive. The Latin de- and scribere are fused; English productively uses -ive, -ion, -ively and -iveness around this stem.
intro.cn: descriptive 是 descript- 加 -ive。拉丁 de- 与 scribere 已融合；英语在这个词干周围能产地使用 -ive、-ion、-ively、-iveness。

latinIntro.en: Latin scribere 'to write' yields describere 'write down', descriptio 'a description', and scriptum 'something written'. English relatives include describe, description, prescribe, subscribe and manuscript.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 scribere“写”派生 describere“写下”、descriptio“描述”、scriptum“写下的东西”。英语同族词包括 describe、description、prescribe、subscribe、manuscript。

items.meaning: to write down; to say what something is like
items.meaningCN: 写下；描述（de-“向下”+ scribere“写”）
items.example: The witness described the car in detail.
items.exampleCN: 证人详细描述了那辆车。

items.meaning: an account of something
items.meaningCN: 描述；说明（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The job description lists the main duties.
items.exampleCN: 职位说明列出了主要职责。

items.meaning: giving an account without judging
items.meaningCN: 描述性的；描写的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The passage is purely descriptive.
items.exampleCN: 这一段纯粹是描写。

items.meaning: in a descriptive manner
items.meaningCN: 描述性地（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: The term is used descriptively, not as criticism.
items.exampleCN: 这个说法是描述性用法，不是批评。

items.meaning: the quality of being descriptive
items.meaningCN: 描述性；描写性（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The descriptiveness of the diary makes it valuable to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记的描写性使它对历史学家很有价值。

items.meaning: to write rules in advance
items.meaningCN: 规定；开处方（pre-“预先”+ scribere“写”）
items.example: The law prescribes a minimum age for the licence.
items.exampleCN: 法律规定该驾照的最低年龄。

items.meaning: to write one's name under; to agree to receive
items.meaningCN: 订阅；签署（sub-“在下”+ scribere“写”）
items.example: She subscribed to two science magazines.
items.exampleCN: 她订阅了两本科学杂志。

items.meaning: a text written by hand
items.meaningCN: 手稿（manu-“手”+ scriptum“写下的东西”）
items.example: The manuscript was revised three times.
items.exampleCN: 手稿修改了三次。

definition_zh: 名称；称号；指定；任命；标示
definition_en: a name or title given to something, or the act of officially choosing or marking it
core_image: 一只手在文件上盖下印章，把一个名字正式按在某块土地上
scene: The site received the designation of protected wetland last year.
sceneCN: 这里 designation 是「（官方）认定、称号」（第 2 个义项：正式指定某物具有某种身份）；句意：该地点去年获得了受保护湿地的认定。图中可辨识物件：湿地、界桩、盖有印章的认定文件、指示牌。

pos.zh: 名称；称号；指定；任命；标示

senses.title: A name or title
senses.titleCN: 名称：给它一个正式的叫法
senses.definition: the name or title by which something is officially known
senses.definitionCN: 某物被正式使用的名称或称号
senses.example: The plant's scientific designation is longer than its common name.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的科学名称比它的俗名长。
senses.why: designare means 'to mark out'. A designation is the mark left on a thing by naming it, so the name becomes the official handle.
senses.whyCN: designare 意为“标出”。designation 是命名在事物上留下的标记，于是这个名字成了官方把手。

senses.title: Official recognition of status
senses.titleCN: 官方认定：给它一个身份
senses.definition: the formal act of declaring that something has a particular status
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某物具有某种身份的行为
senses.example: The designation of the area as a nature reserve blocked new construction.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区被认定为自然保护区后，新建设被阻止。
senses.why: The mark here is legal rather than verbal. Officials designate a site by writing its status into the record, and the status changes what may be done there.
senses.whyCN: 这里的标记是法律性的，而非口头性的。官员把某地的身份写入记录，这个身份就改变了那里允许做什么。

senses.title: Appointment to a post
senses.titleCN: 任命：把人和位子对上
senses.definition: the act of appointing someone to a particular role or office
senses.definitionCN: 把某人任命到某个角色或职位的行为
senses.example: Her designation as chair took effect in January.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为主席，于一月生效。
senses.why: To designate a person for a post is to mark that person as occupying it. The noun names the appointment rather than the person's abilities.
senses.whyCN: 把某人指定到某职位，就是标记此人在其位。名词命名的是任命行为，而非此人的能力。

senses.title: A label or code
senses.titleCN: 代号：一串字符代表它
senses.definition: a short label, code or symbol used to identify something
senses.definitionCN: 用于识别某物的简短标签、代码或符号
senses.example: Each sample carries a designation such as B-14.
senses.exampleCN: 每个样本都带有一个如 B-14 的编号。
senses.why: A code is a mark reduced to its smallest form. The noun still names the identifying mark, even when the mark is only letters and digits.
senses.whyCN: 代码是被压缩到最小形式的标记。即使标记只是字母和数字，这个名词仍命名识别标记。

senses.title: Marking out an area
senses.titleCN: 划定：在地图上圈出这一块
senses.definition: the marking of land or space for a particular use or restriction
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途或限制而标出土地或空间
senses.example: Zoning designations decide which plots may hold factories.
senses.exampleCN: 分区划定决定哪些地块可以建工厂。
senses.why: This sense is almost literal: a boundary is drawn on a map, and the enclosed area is designated. The pen does the work that designare describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项几乎是字面的：地图上画一条界线，圈内的区域就被划定了。笔做的正是 designare 描述的工作。

senses.title: Target marking
senses.titleCN: 目标指定：把要打的东西标出来
senses.definition: in military or technical use, the selection and marking of a target for action
senses.definitionCN: 军事或技术用语中，选定并标出行动目标
senses.example: Laser designation guided the missile to the correct building.
senses.exampleCN: 激光目标指定把导弹引向正确的大楼。
senses.why: A target must be marked before it can be hit. The technical phrase keeps the physical gesture of pointing something out with a mark.
senses.whyCN: 目标必须先被标出才能被击中。这个技术短语保留了“用标记指出某物”的物理手势。

senses.title: A classifying label in taxonomy
senses.titleCN: 分类命名：给物种一个学名
senses.definition: the formal naming of a species or group in scientific classification
senses.definitionCN: 科学分类中为物种或类群正式命名
senses.example: The new beetle received its designation after the museum's founder.
senses.exampleCN: 这种新甲虫以博物馆创始人的名字命名。
senses.why: Scientific naming is marking with precision: the designation fixes a specimen to a category, so that every later record can point to the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 科学命名是精确标记： designation 把标本固定到某个类别，使后来所有记录都指向同一物。

senses.title: The act of pointing out in speech
senses.titleCN: 指称：用词点到那个对象
senses.definition: in philosophy and linguistics, the referring of a term to a particular object
senses.definitionCN: 哲学与语言学中，一个词项指向特定对象
senses.example: The article examines how proper names achieve designation.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章考察专有名词如何实现指称。
senses.why: Designation in this technical sense is pointing with a word. The mark is not on paper but in the relation between a term and its object.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义中的指称是用词来指。标记不在纸上，而在词项与对象之间的关系里。

intro.en: Designation comes from Latin designatio 'a marking out', from designare, de- 'out' plus signare 'to mark' and signum 'a sign'. The word has always meant putting a mark on something to identify it.
intro.cn: designation 来自拉丁 designatio“标出”，来自 designare，由 de-“出”加 signare“标记”和 signum“记号”构成。这个词一直表示在某物上留下识别标记。

items.en: signum meant 'a mark, sign, token'. It is the source of sign, signal and signature, so the family is about visible marks that carry meaning.
items.cn: signum 意为“标记、记号、信物”。它是 sign、signal、signature 的来源，因此这个词族关乎承载意义的可见标记。

items.en: signare 'to mark, seal, sign' turns the noun into a verb. A seal pressed into wax is the clearest image: a mark that makes a claim official.
items.cn: signare“标记、盖章、签名”把名词变成动词。压进蜡里的印章是最清楚的画面：一个使主张生效的标记。

items.en: designare adds de- 'out, completely' to signare, giving 'to mark out, point out, appoint'. Latin used it for choosing a successor as well as for drawing boundaries.
items.cn: designare 给 signare 加 de-“出、完全”，意为“标出、指出、指定”。拉丁语既用它表示选定继任者，也表示划界。

items.en: designatio named the act of marking out and the mark produced. English borrowed the stem designation- and formed the noun with -ion.
items.cn: designatio 命名标出的动作及产生的标记。英语借入 designation- 词干，用 -ion 构成名词。

items.en: English uses designation from the 15th century for a name, appointment or boundary. The exact first record is uncertain because designate entered separately.
items.cn: 英语从 15 世纪起用 designation 表示名称、任命或界线。由于 designate 是另行进入的，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: In the 20th century the word spread to zoning, taxonomy, military targeting and philosophy of language. Each field marks a different kind of object with a name.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到分区规划、分类学、军事目标指定和语言哲学。每个领域都用名称标记不同种类的对象。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sign- stem through different prefixes and endings; the near-meaning group separates naming, appointing, marking and classifying.
note.cn: 形近组经不同前缀与词尾共享 sign- 词干；近义组区分命名、任命、标记与分类。

entries.definition: to officially choose, name or mark; the verb names the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 正式选定、命名或标出；这个动词命名名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: serving to designate or point out; the -ive suffix turns the action into a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 用于指称或标示的；-ive 后缀把动作变成性质。

entries.definition: a plan or pattern; it shares signum but shifted from 'mark out' to 'plan out' in English.
entries.definitionCN: 设计；图案；方案。它共享 signum，但在英语中从“标出”转变为“规划出”。

entries.definition: the word by which a person or thing is known; a designation is more formal and often official.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物被称呼的词；designation 更正式，常带官方色彩。

entries.definition: a name showing rank or office; it is narrower than designation, which also covers codes and statuses.
entries.definitionCN: 显示等级或职位的名称；比 designation 窄，后者也包括代号与身份认定。

entries.definition: the act of choosing someone for a position; it matches sense 3 but does not cover naming or marking.
entries.definitionCN: 选定某人担任职位；对应第 3 义，但不涵盖命名或标记。

entries.definition: the act of arranging things into classes; designation names the label, classification names the system.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物分入类别的行为；designation 命名标签，classification 命名体系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'out' + signum 'mark': designation is a mark put out where everyone can read it.
normal.cn: de-“出”+ signum“记号”：designation 是摆出来给所有人读的标记。

normal.en: sign, signal, signature and designate all share signum; the family is about visible marks.
normal.cn: sign、signal、signature、designate 都共享 signum，这个词族关乎可见标记。

normal.en: The usual pattern is designation as: the mark names the new status.
normal.cn: 常用结构是 designation as：标记命名了新身份。

normal.en: In planning, remember land designation: the map mark decides what may be built.
normal.cn: 规划中记住 land designation：地图上的标记决定能建什么。

normal.en: A sample designation is just a code, so the word works at every scale from species to test tube.
normal.cn: sample designation 只是一个代号，因此这个词从物种到试管各个尺度都适用。

abstract.en: Think of a rubber stamp coming down on a document and leaving a name in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象橡皮图章落在文件上，用墨留下一个名字。

abstract.en: Think of a surveyor driving a stake into the ground to fix a boundary.
abstract.cn: 想象测量员把木桩打进地里，固定一条界线。

abstract.en: Think of a museum label beside a specimen: the object is already there; the label only points.
abstract.cn: 想象标本旁的博物馆标签：物件早已在那里，标签只负责指出来。

examples.en: The official designation of the building as a monument saved it from demolition.
examples.cn: 该建筑被正式认定为文物，从而免于拆除。

examples.en: Each chemical in the catalogue has a short designation for lab use.
examples.cn: 目录中的每种化学品都有一个实验室用的简短代号。

examples.en: Her designation as head of department was announced in March.
examples.cn: 她被任命为系主任的消息在三月公布。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地signation”——地（de）上插一个 sign（标记），正式写明这块地叫什么 → designation 名称、指定

root: 拉丁 designatio“标出、指定” ← designare（de-“出”+ signare“标记”，源自 signum“记号”）；designat- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one act: a mark is made so that a person, place or thing can be identified and treated in a particular way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：留下标记，使人、地点或事物能被识别并按特定方式对待。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed onto a document, fixing a name to a place.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章压在文件上，把一个名字固定到一处。

branches.en: NAME AND CODE: a full title and a short code are the same identifying mark at different lengths.
branches.cn: 名称与代号：完整称号与简短代码，是同一识别标记的不同长度。

branches.en: SPACE: zoning a plot writes a mark that changes what is permitted.
branches.cn: 空间：划定一块土地，写下改变许可范围的标记。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND TARGETS: appointing a person and marking a target both point an institution at the object it must act on.
branches.cn: 人与目标：任命一个人与标定一个目标，都把机构指向它必须作用的对象。

branches.en: SCIENCE AND LANGUAGE: a taxonomic name and a referring term both tie a label to one specific object.
branches.cn: 科学与语言：分类学名与指称词项，都把标签系到某个特定对象。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL CORE: the legal act of designating is the model for all the other senses, because it makes the mark binding.
branches.cn: 官方核心：法律上的认定行为是其他义项的模型，因为它使标记具有约束力。

intro.en: Designation is designat- plus -ion. The Latin de- and signum are fused inside the stem; English adds -ion, -ive and -ed productively.
intro.cn: designation 是 designat- 加 -ion。拉丁 de- 与 signum 已融合在词干内；英语能产地加 -ion、-ive 和 -ed。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum 'mark' yields signare 'to mark', designare 'to mark out', and designatio 'a marking out'. English relatives include sign, signal, signature, design and designate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 signum“记号”派生 signare“标记”、designare“标出”、designatio“标出”。英语同族词包括 sign、signal、signature、design、designate。

items.meaning: to mark out; to name or appoint officially
items.meaningCN: 标出；正式命名或指定（de-“出”+ signare“标记”）
items.example: The council designated the old mill as a heritage site.
items.exampleCN: 议会把老磨坊指定为遗产地。

items.meaning: the act of marking out, or the name given
items.meaningCN: 指定；名称（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The designation appears on every official map.
items.exampleCN: 这个名称出现在每一张官方地图上。

items.meaning: serving to point out or name
items.meaningCN: 指称的；标示的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The phrase has a designative rather than descriptive function.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语起指称作用，而不是描述作用。

items.meaning: officially named or set aside
items.meaningCN: 被指定的；被划定的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: Park only in the designated areas.
items.exampleCN: 只能在指定区域停车。

items.meaning: to plan out; a plan or pattern
items.meaningCN: 设计；图案（由“标出”转为“规划出”）
items.example: The garden design uses straight lines.
items.exampleCN: 这个花园设计使用直线。

items.meaning: a person who designs
items.meaningCN: 设计者（-er 构成施事者名词）
items.example: The designer chose a lighter material.
items.exampleCN: 设计师选择了更轻的材料。

items.meaning: a visible mark with meaning
items.meaningCN: 记号；标志（同源词）
items.example: A red sign marked the danger zone.
items.exampleCN: 一块红色标志标出了危险区。

items.meaning: a sign that conveys information
items.meaningCN: 信号（同源词，承载信息的记号）
items.example: The radio signal was weak in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 山谷里的无线电信号很弱。

definition_zh: 发现；察觉；探测；检测；侦查
definition_en: the act of discovering or noticing something that is hidden, faint or not yet known
core_image: 一只手掀开盖布，下面的东西第一次露出来
scene: Early detection of the leak saved the plant from a costly shutdown.
sceneCN: 这里 detection 是「检测、发现」（第 5 个义项：发现隐藏的故障）；句意：及早检测出泄漏，使工厂免于代价高昂的停产。图中可辨识物件：管道、压力表、渗出的水迹、检修手电。

pos.zh: 发现；察觉；探测；检测；侦查

senses.title: Discovering what was hidden
senses.titleCN: 发现：盖子被揭开
senses.definition: the act of finding or noticing something that was concealed or not immediately obvious
senses.definitionCN: 发现或注意到被隐藏或不明显之物的行为
senses.example: The detection of a second entrance changed the whole investigation.
senses.exampleCN: 第二个入口的发现改变了整个调查。
senses.why: detegere means 'to uncover', de- 'un-' plus tegere 'to cover'. Detection is the moment a cover comes off and something underneath becomes known.
senses.whyCN: detegere 意为“揭开”，由 de-“去除”和 tegere“覆盖”构成。detection 就是盖子被揭开、下面的东西被知道的那一刻。

senses.title: Sensing a weak signal
senses.titleCN: 探测：把微弱信号从噪声里捞出来
senses.definition: the process of discovering a signal, particle or object by means of an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 借助仪器发现信号、粒子或物体的过程
senses.example: The detection of gravitational waves required extremely sensitive mirrors.
senses.exampleCN: 引力波的探测需要极其灵敏的镜面。
senses.why: An instrument uncovers what the senses cannot. The word keeps the uncovering image even when the cover is noise rather than cloth.
senses.whyCN: 仪器揭开了感官揭不开的东西。即使“覆盖物”是噪声而不是布，这个词仍保留揭盖意象。

senses.title: Police work of finding offenders
senses.titleCN: 侦查：把藏起来的线索挖出来
senses.definition: the work of discovering crimes or offenders
senses.definitionCN: 发现犯罪或罪犯的工作
senses.example: Better detection of fraud reduced losses at the agency.
senses.exampleCN: 更有力的欺诈侦查减少了该机构的损失。
senses.why: Detection in policing is the same uncovering: offenders and evidence are hidden by design, and the investigator removes the cover.
senses.whyCN: 警务中的 detection 是同样的揭开：罪犯与证据被刻意藏起，调查者把覆盖物拿掉。

senses.title: Finding disease early
senses.titleCN: 疾病检测：在症状出现前发现
senses.definition: the identification of a disease or condition, especially before symptoms appear
senses.definitionCN: 识别疾病或状况，尤指在症状出现之前
senses.example: Screening allows detection of the condition at an earlier stage.
senses.exampleCN: 筛查使这种状况能在更早阶段被发现。
senses.why: A disease hides inside the body; detection brings it into view. The medical phrase early detection assumes the cover is time itself.
senses.whyCN: 疾病藏在身体里，detection 把它带入视野。医学短语 early detection 假定的覆盖物就是时间。

senses.title: Finding a leak or fault
senses.titleCN: 检漏：找出看不见的破口
senses.definition: the discovery of a leak, crack or fault in a system
senses.definitionCN: 发现系统中泄漏、裂缝或故障
senses.example: Gas detection sensors line the tunnel ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道顶部沿线装有气体检测传感器。
senses.why: A fault is covered by metal or concrete. Detection removes that cover with instruments, so maintenance can begin.
senses.whyCN: 故障被金属或混凝土覆盖。detection 用仪器拿掉这层覆盖，维修才得以开始。

senses.title: Spotting fraud or error
senses.titleCN: 识别：把假的挑出来
senses.definition: the identification of fraud, error or irregularity in records or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 在记录或行为中识别欺诈、错误或不正常之处
senses.example: Automatic detection of duplicate claims saved the insurer millions.
senses.exampleCN: 重复索赔的自动识别为保险公司省下数百万。
senses.why: Irregularities are covered by ordinary-looking entries. Detection uncovers the pattern beneath the surface.
senses.whyCN: 异常被看似正常的条目盖住。detection 揭开表面之下的模式。

senses.title: The technical threshold
senses.titleCN: 检测限：低到这个程度才看得见
senses.definition: the point at which an instrument can just distinguish something from background
senses.definitionCN: 仪器刚好能把某物与本底区分开的那一点
senses.example: The detection limit of the sensor is one part per billion.
senses.exampleCN: 该传感器的检测限是十亿分之一。
senses.why: This sense names the edge of uncovering: below it, the cover stays on. The noun shifts from the act to the measurable boundary of the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项命名揭盖的边缘：低于它，盖子仍盖着。名词从动作转指动作的可测边界。

senses.title: Noticing a change
senses.titleCN: 察觉变化：从平静里看出不同
senses.definition: the recognition that something has changed or is present, often during monitoring
senses.definitionCN: 在监测中意识到某物已变化或已出现
senses.example: Detection of a slight temperature rise warned the operators.
senses.exampleCN: 温度轻微上升的察觉给操作员发出了警告。
senses.why: Monitoring compares a current reading with an earlier one. The difference is the thing uncovered, and noticing it is detection.
senses.whyCN: 监测把当前读数与先前读数比较。差异就是被揭开之物，注意到它就是 detection。

intro.en: Detection comes from Latin detectio, from detegere 'to uncover', de- 'un-' plus tegere 'to cover'. The word entered English through French and moved from literal uncovering to technical sensing.
intro.cn: detection 来自拉丁 detectio，来自 detegere“揭开”，由 de-“去除”和 tegere“覆盖”构成。这个词经法语进入英语，从字面揭开转向技术探测。

items.en: tegere meant 'to cover, hide'. It also gives protect (pro- 'in front' + tegere) and integument, so the family is about what lies over something else.
items.cn: tegere 意为“覆盖、隐藏”。它还派生了 protect（pro-“在前”+ tegere）和 integument，因此这个词族关乎覆盖在他物之上的东西。

items.en: detegere adds de- 'un-, off', giving 'to uncover, expose'. Latin used it for removing a physical covering and for revealing a secret.
items.cn: detegere 加 de-“去除”，意为“揭开、暴露”。拉丁语既用它表示移除实物覆盖，也表示揭露秘密。

items.en: detectio named the act of uncovering. The stem detect- passes into French and then English, where the noun appears in the 15th century; exact dating is uncertain.
items.cn: detectio 命名揭开的动作。detect- 词干经法语传入英语，名词在 15 世纪出现，确切年代存疑。

items.en: Early English use is often legal or investigative: detecting a crime means uncovering what was concealed. The modern detective keeps this sense.
items.cn: 早期英语用法常与法律或调查有关：detect a crime 意为揭开被隐藏之事。现代 detective 保留了这个义项。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries, instruments extended detection to signals, particles and chemicals. The cover became whatever prevents human senses from noticing.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，仪器把 detection 扩展到信号、粒子和化学物质。覆盖物变成任何阻止人类感官察觉的东西。

items.en: Early detection became a medical slogan, and fraud detection a digital one. Both keep the same promise: find what is hidden before it does harm.
items.cn: early detection 成为医学口号，fraud detection 成为数字领域口号。两者都保留同一个承诺：在隐藏之物造成伤害前找到它。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the detect- stem with different endings; the near-meaning group separates discovering, sensing, diagnosing and identifying.
note.cn: 形近组共享 detect- 词干、词尾不同；近义组区分发现、感知、诊断与识别。

entries.definition: to discover or notice something hidden; the verb names the uncovering act.
entries.definitionCN: 发现或注意到隐藏之物；这个动词命名揭开的动作。

entries.definition: a person whose job is to solve crimes; the -ive ending marks the role rather than the process.
entries.definitionCN: 以侦破案件为职业的人；-ive 词尾标记角色而非过程。

entries.definition: an instrument that detects something; the -or suffix marks the doer, here a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 用于探测某物的仪器；-or 后缀标记施事者，这里是机器。

entries.definition: the act of finding something for the first time; it is broader than detection and need not involve concealment.
entries.definitionCN: 首次发现某物；比 detection 宽，不必涉及隐藏。

entries.definition: the act of recognising and naming something; detection finds it, identification says what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 识别并命名某物；detection 找到它，identification 说明它是什么。

entries.definition: the continuous reading of a physical quantity by a device; it may not involve discovering anything new.
entries.definitionCN: 装置对物理量的连续读取；不一定涉及发现新事物。

entries.definition: the identification of a disease from its signs; detection finds the condition, diagnosis names and explains it.
entries.definitionCN: 根据征象识别疾病；detection 发现状况，diagnosis 命名并解释它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'un-' + tegere 'cover': detection is the cover coming off.
normal.cn: de-“去除”+ tegere“覆盖”：detection 就是覆盖物被拿掉。

normal.en: protect is the same root with pro- 'in front': protection puts a cover on, detection takes one off.
normal.cn: protect 是同一词根加 pro-“在前”：保护是盖上，检测是揭开。

normal.en: The medical phrase is early detection, because the value lies in finding the hidden condition before symptoms.
normal.cn: 医学搭配是 early detection，因为价值在于症状出现前发现隐藏状况。

normal.en: A detector is the machine, a detective the person, and detection the act; keep the three endings apart.
normal.cn: detector 是机器，detective 是人，detection 是行为；三个词尾要分清。

normal.en: Detection limit is the line below which the cover stays on, so the phrase is about the edge of uncovering.
normal.cn: detection limit 是盖子仍然盖着的界线，因此这个短语讲的是揭开的边缘。

abstract.en: Think of a sheet pulled off a sculpture at an unveiling: the shape was there all along.
abstract.cn: 想象揭幕时布从雕塑上被拉开：形状一直都在。

abstract.en: Think of a smoke alarm hearing what no one in the house can hear.
abstract.cn: 想象烟雾报警器听见了屋里谁都听不到的东西。

abstract.en: Think of a torch beam finding a crack in a dark wall: the crack existed, the light made it known.
abstract.cn: 想象手电光在暗墙上找到一条裂缝：裂缝本来就在，光让它被知道。

examples.en: The detection of the virus in wastewater gave officials an early warning.
examples.cn: 在废水中检测出病毒，给官员提供了早期预警。

examples.en: Improved detection methods cut the number of missed cases.
examples.cn: 改进的检测方法减少了漏诊数量。

examples.en: The thief escaped detection by wearing a uniform.
examples.cn: 那名窃贼靠穿制服躲过了侦查。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地take身”——地（de）上把盖布 take（拿）走，藏着的身体就露出来了 → detection 发现、探测

root: 拉丁 detegere“揭开”（de-“去除”+ tegere“覆盖”）；detect- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one moment: a cover is removed and something previously out of sight becomes known.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个瞬间：覆盖物被移除，先前看不见的东西变得可知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth lifted off an object that was hidden underneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖布被掀开，下面的物件露出来。

branches.en: FORENSIC: solving a crime is the same removal of a deliberate cover.
branches.cn: 侦查：侦破案件是移除刻意设置的覆盖。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS AND LIMITS: a detector uncovers a weak signal, and the detection limit marks where uncovering stops.
branches.cn: 仪器与极限：探测器揭开微弱信号，检测限标记揭开停止之处。

branches.en: BODY AND MACHINE: disease and leaks are both hidden inside something, and both are found before harm spreads.
branches.cn: 身体与机器：疾病与泄漏都藏在某物内部，都在伤害扩散前被发现。

branches.en: PATTERNS AND CHANGES: fraud hides behind normal entries, and a small change hides inside steady readings.
branches.cn: 模式与变化：欺诈躲在正常条目后面，微小变化藏在稳定读数里。

branches.en: THE BASE ACT: every sense is a removal of whatever prevented knowledge, whether cloth, noise, time or habit.
branches.cn: 基础动作：每个义项都是移除阻碍认知之物——无论是布、噪声、时间还是习惯。

intro.en: Detection is detect plus -ion. The Latin de- and tegere are fused inside detect; English adds -ion, -ive, -or and -able productively.
intro.cn: detection 是 detect 加 -ion。拉丁 de- 与 tegere 已融合在 detect 内；英语能产地加 -ion、-ive、-or、-able。

latinIntro.en: Latin tegere 'to cover' yields detegere 'uncover', protectus 'covered in front', and tectum 'a roof'. English relatives include detect, protect, tegument and tile through French tuile.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tegere“覆盖”派生 detegere“揭开”、protectus“在前遮挡”、tectum“屋顶”。英语同族词包括 detect、protect、tegument，以及经法语 tuile 而来的 tile。

items.meaning: to uncover; to discover
items.meaningCN: 发现；探测（de-“去除”+ tegere“覆盖”）
items.example: The sensor can detect very small movements.
items.exampleCN: 这个传感器能探测极小的移动。

items.meaning: the act of discovering something hidden
items.meaningCN: 发现；检测（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Detection of the fault took less than a second.
items.exampleCN: 故障检测用了不到一秒。

items.meaning: a person who investigates crimes
items.meaningCN: 侦探（-ive 构成人物名词）
items.example: The detective re-examined the locked room.
items.exampleCN: 侦探重新检查了那间锁着的房间。

items.meaning: an instrument that detects
items.meaningCN: 探测器；检测器（-or 构成施事者名词）
items.example: The metal detector sounded at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 金属探测器在门口响了。

items.meaning: able to be detected
items.meaningCN: 可检测的（-able“能够被……”）
items.example: The difference was barely detectable.
items.exampleCN: 这个差别几乎检测不到。

items.meaning: not discovered
items.meaningCN: 未被发现的（un-“不”+ detected）
items.example: The error went undetected for years.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误多年未被发现。

items.meaning: to cover in front; to shield
items.meaningCN: 保护；防护（pro-“在前”+ tegere“覆盖”）
items.example: The coating protects the metal from rust.
items.exampleCN: 涂层保护金属不生锈。

items.meaning: a natural covering
items.meaningCN: 外皮；天然覆盖层（-mentum 构成事物名词）
items.example: The tegument of the parasite protects it inside the host.
items.exampleCN: 这种寄生虫的外皮在宿主体内保护它。

definition_en: firmness of purpose, or the act of establishing something precisely or deciding it officially
core_image: 一条线被牢牢钉在地图的边界上，不再移动
scene: Her determination carried the team through two years of failed experiments.
sceneCN: 这里 determination 是「决心」（第 1 个义项：不改变目标的意志）；句意：她的决心带着团队熬过了两年失败的实验。图中可辨识物件：实验台、记录本上划掉的方案、深夜的灯、握紧的拳头。

senses.title: Firmness of purpose
senses.titleCN: 决心：不改目标
senses.definition: the quality of continuing to pursue a goal despite difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 面对困难仍继续追求目标的品质
senses.example: Her determination kept the project alive after the first failure.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次失败后，她的决心让项目继续存活。
senses.why: determinare means 'to set a boundary'. A determined person has fixed the limit of how far they will go, so the will does not drift.
senses.whyCN: determinare 意为“定界”。有 determination 的人已经定好自己要走多远的边界，因此意志不会漂移。

senses.title: Measuring a value precisely
senses.titleCN: 测定：把数值定下来
senses.definition: the act of finding out a quantity, quality or value exactly
senses.definitionCN: 准确查明某数量、性质或数值的行为
senses.example: The determination of the sample's age used two independent methods.
senses.exampleCN: 样本年龄的测定用了两种独立方法。
senses.why: To determine a value is to set its boundary on a scale: once measured, the number is fixed rather than approximate.
senses.whyCN: 测定一个值，就是在标尺上定出它的边界：一旦测出，数字就被固定，而不再是大概。

senses.title: An official decision
senses.titleCN: 裁定：由有权者拍板
senses.definition: a formal decision made by an authority after considering a matter
senses.definitionCN: 有权机关在审议后作出的正式决定
senses.example: The board's determination ended the dispute over the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会的裁定结束了这场合同争议。
senses.why: An authority fixes the endpoint of a debate. The noun names that act of setting the boundary beyond which argument may not go.
senses.whyCN: 权威为争论定下终点。这个名词命名的是划定边界、使争论不得越过的行为。

senses.title: Establishing the facts
senses.titleCN: 查明：把事实钉牢
senses.definition: the act of establishing what is true about a situation or cause
senses.definitionCN: 确立关于某情况或原因之真相的行为
senses.example: The determination of the cause took months of testing.
senses.exampleCN: 查明原因花了数月测试。
senses.why: Investigation narrows possibilities until one cause remains inside the boundary. Determination is the closing of that boundary.
senses.whyCN: 调查不断缩小可能性，直到边界内只剩一个原因。determination 就是这条边界合拢。

senses.title: A legal ruling
senses.titleCN: 法律裁决：把权利定清
senses.definition: a judicial decision that settles a question of law or fact
senses.definitionCN: 解决法律或事实问题的司法决定
senses.example: The court's determination set the boundary between the two properties.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的裁决确定了两处房产之间的界线。
senses.why: Law is where the root is most visible: a determination literally draws a line that both parties must accept.
senses.whyCN: 法律是词根最可见的领域：一项 determination 字面上画出一条双方都必须接受的线。

senses.title: Defining a limit or character
senses.titleCN: 界定：说清边界与性质
senses.definition: the act of fixing the limits, nature or meaning of something
senses.definitionCN: 确定某物的范围、性质或意义的行为
senses.example: The determination of the region's borders took years of negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区边界的界定花了多年谈判。
senses.why: Here determination is definition in the literal sense: de- 'completely' plus terminare 'to bound'. The edge is drawn, not discovered.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 determination 就是字面意义上的定义：de-“完全”加 terminare“定界”。边界是被画出的，而不是被发现的。

senses.title: Solving for a result
senses.titleCN: 判定求解：让答案唯一
senses.definition: the process of fixing a unique result from given conditions, as in mathematics or computation
senses.definitionCN: 在给定条件下确定唯一结果的过程，如数学或计算中
senses.example: The algorithm's determination of the shortest path is guaranteed to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 该算法对最短路径的判定保证会结束。
senses.why: Given conditions bound the possible answers; determination selects the one inside the boundary, so the result is fixed rather than optional.
senses.whyCN: 给定条件限定了可能答案；determination 选出边界内那一个，于是结果是固定的而非可选的。

senses.title: Biological fate-setting
senses.titleCN: 分化决定：细胞注定成为什么
senses.definition: in biology, the process by which a cell's future identity becomes fixed
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中细胞未来身份被固定的过程
senses.example: Cell determination happens before the tissue visibly changes.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞分化决定在组织出现可见变化之前就已发生。
senses.why: A cell's options are narrowed until only one fate remains. The word is apt because the boundary is set before the outcome can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 细胞的选择被收窄，直到只剩一种命运。这个词用得贴切，因为边界在结果可见之前就已设定。

intro.en: Determination comes from Latin determinatio, from determinare 'to set bounds', de- 'completely' plus terminare 'to limit', from terminus 'boundary'. Every sense still involves fixing an edge.
intro.cn: determination 来自拉丁 determinatio，来自 determinare“定界”，由 de-“完全”加 terminare“限定”构成，而 terminus 意为“边界”。每个义项都仍涉及固定一条边。

items.en: terminus meant 'a boundary stone, limit, end'. It also gives terminal and terminate, so the family is about where something stops.
items.cn: terminus 意为“界石、界限、终点”。它也派生了 terminal 和 terminate，因此这个词族关乎事物在哪里停止。

items.en: terminare 'to set a limit, bring to an end' turns the boundary stone into an action. To terminate is to put an end to something.
items.cn: terminare“定界、使结束”把界石变成动作。terminate 就是给某事画上终点。

items.en: determinare adds de- 'completely', giving 'to bound fully, settle, decide'. Latin used it for fixing a price, a date or a question.
items.cn: determinare 加 de-“完全”，意为“彻底定界、确定、决定”。拉丁语用它确定价格、日期或问题。

items.en: English adopts determination in the 14th century, first for a decision or conclusion. The exact earliest record is uncertain because determine entered through French at the same period.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪采用 determination，最初表示决定或结论。由于 determine 同期经法语进入，确切最早记录存疑。

items.en: In the 17th and 18th centuries, science used determination for the exact measurement of a quantity, keeping the sense of a value fixed within limits.
items.cn: 17 至 18 世纪，科学用 determination 表示对某量的精确测量，保留了“值被固定在界限内”的含义。

items.en: Developmental biology in the 20th century named cell determination: a cell's future is fixed before it visibly differentiates. The boundary is set early.
items.cn: 20 世纪的发育生物学命名了 cell determination：细胞的未来在可见分化之前就被固定。边界很早就设定了。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the termin- stem with different endings; the near-meaning group separates resolve, measurement, decision and verdict.
note.cn: 形近组共享 termin- 词干、词尾不同；近义组区分毅力、测量、决定与裁决。

entries.definition: to decide, establish or measure; the verb names the act of setting the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 决定、确定或测定；这个动词命名设定边界的动作。

entries.definition: having firm purpose, or having been fixed; it describes a person or a result, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 坚决的，或已被确定的；它描述人或结果，而非过程。

entries.definition: a factor that decides an outcome, or a value computed from a matrix; the -ant ending marks the deciding element.
entries.definitionCN: 决定结果的因素，或由矩阵算出的值；-ant 词尾标记起决定作用的成分。

entries.definition: strong determination to do something; it stresses the inner decision rather than the outer goal.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的坚定决心；它强调内在决意，而非外在目标。

entries.definition: the act of measuring; a determination in science is a measurement made exact and final.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的行为；科学中的 determination 是做到精确且最终的测量。

entries.definition: a choice reached after consideration; determination may also mean the official act of settling a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 考虑后作出的选择；determination 也可指正式了结某事的裁定。

entries.definition: a formal decision by a jury or judge; narrower than determination, which also covers administrative rulings.
entries.definitionCN: 陪审团或法官的正式裁决；比 determination 窄，后者也涵盖行政裁定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: terminus 'boundary' + de- 'completely': determination is a boundary set all the way round.
normal.cn: terminus“边界”+ de-“完全”：determination 是四面都定好的边界。

normal.en: terminal and terminate are cousins: all three words are about where something stops.
normal.cn: terminal 与 terminate 是表亲：三个词都关乎事物在哪里停止。

normal.en: In science the phrase is 'the determination of a value', which tells you the boundary is numerical.
normal.cn: 科学中的搭配是 the determination of a value，说明这里的边界是数值。

normal.en: Self-determination is the same word turned inward: a people sets its own boundary.
normal.cn: self-determination 是同一个词转向内部：一个民族自己设定边界。

normal.en: In law, a determination is a line both parties must accept, which is why the word feels final.
normal.cn: 法律中的 determination 是双方都必须接受的线，因此这个词带有终局感。

abstract.en: Think of a surveyor's stake driven into the ground and declared unmovable.
abstract.cn: 想象测量员的木桩打进地里，被宣布不可移动。

abstract.en: Think of a climber who has fixed the summit as the only acceptable end point.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者把顶峰定为唯一可接受的终点。

abstract.en: Think of a ruler laid on a map and a line drawn in ink: after that, the border exists.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子压在地图上，用墨画下一条线：此后边界就存在了。

examples.en: The determination of the water's lead content took three separate tests.
examples.cn: 水中铅含量的测定做了三次独立检测。

examples.en: Her determination to finish the marathon surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 她跑完马拉松的决心让所有人惊讶。

examples.en: The tribunal's determination is binding on both companies.
examples.cn: 仲裁庭的裁定对两家公司都有约束力。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地特mination”——地（de）上特别（ter）明确地画出 min（最小）边界，不再更改 → determination 决心、测定、裁定

root: 拉丁 determinare“彻底定界”（de-“完全”+ terminare“限定”，源自 terminus“边界”）；determinat- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one act: a boundary is fixed, so that will, value, fact or fate can no longer drift.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：边界被固定，于是意志、数值、事实或命运不再漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary line pinned down and declared final.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界线被钉住，宣布为最终。

branches.en: OUTWARD FIXING: a solution that must be unique is an edge held firm.
branches.cn: 向外固定：必须唯一的结果，是被牢牢守住的边界。

branches.en: NUMBERS AND DEFINITIONS: measuring a value and defining a region both put a precise edge on something vague.
branches.cn: 数值与定义：测定一个值与界定一个区域，都给模糊之物加上精确边界。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATIVE AND JUDICIAL: a board ruling and a court ruling both end argument by fixing the line.
branches.cn: 行政与司法：董事会裁定与法院裁决都通过固定界线来终结争论。

branches.en: FACT AND FATE: establishing a cause and fixing a cell's future both narrow possibilities until one remains.
branches.cn: 事实与命运：查明原因与固定细胞未来，都把可能性收窄到只剩一个。

branches.en: THE BASE ACT: every extension is a different material being bounded, from will to measurement to fate.
branches.cn: 基础动作：每个引申都是不同材料被定界——从意志到测量再到命运。

intro.en: Determination is determinat- plus -ion. Latin de- and terminus are fused; English adds -ion, -ed, -ate, -ant and -ative productively.
intro.cn: determination 是 determinat- 加 -ion。拉丁 de- 与 terminus 已融合；英语能产地加 -ion、-ed、-ate、-ant、-ative。

latinIntro.en: Latin terminus 'boundary' yields terminare 'to limit', determinare 'to bound fully', and determinatio 'a settling'. English relatives include terminal, terminate, determine and determinant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 terminus“边界”派生 terminare“限定”、determinare“彻底定界”、determinatio“确定”。英语同族词包括 terminal、terminate、determine、determinant。

items.meaning: to decide; to fix; to find out exactly
items.meaningCN: 决定；确定；测定（de-“完全”+ terminare“限定”）
items.example: The test will determine whether the water is safe.
items.exampleCN: 这项检测将确定水是否安全。

items.meaning: the act of fixing; firmness of purpose
items.meaningCN: 确定；测定；决心（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The determination of the boundary took two surveys.
items.exampleCN: 边界的确定做了两次勘测。

items.meaning: firm in purpose; fixed
items.meaningCN: 坚决的；已确定的（-ed 构成分词形容词）
items.example: She was determined to finish before dark.
items.exampleCN: 她决心在天黑前完成。

items.meaning: having definite limits
items.meaningCN: 确定的；有明确界限的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: The process has a determinate end point.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程有一个确定的终点。

items.meaning: a deciding factor; a matrix value
items.meaningCN: 决定因素；行列式（-ant 构成事物名词）
items.example: Cost was the main determinant of the choice.
items.exampleCN: 成本是这一选择的主要决定因素。

items.meaning: serving to decide or limit
items.meaningCN: 决定性的；限定性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The first clause is determinative of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 第一个分句对意义起决定作用。

items.meaning: to bring to an end
items.meaningCN: 终止；结束（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The company terminated the contract early.
items.exampleCN: 公司提前终止了合同。

items.meaning: at the end; an end point
items.meaningCN: 末端的；终点（-al 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: The terminal station is two stops away.
items.exampleCN: 终点站还有两站。

latinEntries.meaning: to set a limit; to end
a fixing of limits; a decision

definition_zh: 发展的；发育的；开发性的
definition_en: relating to the growth, change or gradual formation of a person, system or economy
core_image: 一株幼苗一节一节长高，每一节都比上一节更成熟
scene: The clinic monitors developmental milestones in premature babies.
sceneCN: 这里 developmental 是「发育的」（第 2 个义项：与身体或能力逐步成长有关）；句意：这家诊所监测早产儿的发育里程碑。图中可辨识物件：婴儿秤、身高尺、里程碑记录表、玩具。

pos.zh: 发展的；发育的；开发性的

senses.title: Relating to growth over time
senses.titleCN: 发展的：一步步长起来
senses.definition: concerned with the process by which something grows or changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 与某物随时间成长或变化的过程有关的
senses.example: The report traces the developmental history of the city's transport system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告追溯了该市交通系统的发展史。
senses.why: Development is the noun, and -al makes a relational adjective: the word does not describe a thing but points to the process behind it.
senses.whyCN: development 是名词，-al 构成关系形容词：这个词不描述事物本身，而指向其背后的过程。

senses.title: Physical and mental growth
senses.titleCN: 发育的：身体和能力在长成
senses.definition: relating to the physical, cognitive or emotional growth of a person
senses.definitionCN: 与人身体、认知或情感的成长有关的
senses.example: Premature birth can affect developmental progress in the first years.
senses.exampleCN: 早产可能影响最初几年的发育进程。
senses.why: Here the process is biological unfolding. Each stage prepares the next, which is why paediatricians speak of developmental milestones.
senses.whyCN: 这里的过程是生物性的展开。每个阶段为下一阶段做准备，因此儿科医生会说 developmental milestones。

senses.title: A stage in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 发展阶段的：处在第几节
senses.definition: belonging to a particular point in a sequence of growth or change
senses.definitionCN: 属于成长或变化序列中某一特定时点的
senses.example: Play is a developmental stage that children pass through at different speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏是儿童以不同速度经历的发育阶段。
senses.why: A sequence has joints. The adjective marks which joint of the growth sequence is being discussed, not the whole sequence.
senses.whyCN: 序列有节点。这个形容词标记正在讨论的是成长序列的哪一个节点，而不是整个序列。

senses.title: A delay or disorder in growth
senses.titleCN: 发育（迟缓）的：该到的点没到
senses.definition: describing conditions in which normal growth or skill acquisition is delayed
senses.definitionCN: 描述正常成长或技能习得被延迟的状况
senses.example: Early therapy can reduce the impact of a developmental delay.
senses.exampleCN: 早期治疗可以减轻发育迟缓的影响。
senses.why: The adjective names the axis on which the problem lies: not behaviour alone, but the timetable of growth itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名问题所在的轴：不只是行为，而是成长的时间表本身。

senses.title: Economic development policy
senses.titleCN: 发展（经济）的：国家如何长大
senses.definition: relating to policies or institutions that promote economic and social development
senses.definitionCN: 与促进经济和社会发展的政策或制度有关的
senses.example: The developmental state model gave the government a strong planning role.
senses.exampleCN: 发展型国家模式赋予政府强有力的规划角色。
